## Dev artifact name

When other projects consume the built artifact (e.g. the installed CLI) while this repo is under
active development, the dev build installs under a separate name so a mid-cycle install never
clobbers the binary consumers are running:

- **Name**: the manifest's package name carries a `-dev` suffix (`<name>` -> `<name>-dev`). If Rust,
  `[package].name`, so the per-commit flow's `cargo install` produces `<name>-dev` and leaves plain
  `<name>` untouched.
- **Constant, not per-step**: the step already lives in the version-of-record (`<name>-dev -V`
  reports the exact rung). A per-step name would churn the manifest every commit and litter the
  install dir with stale binaries.
- **Promotion**: plain `<name>` updates only by an explicit act: a separate clone built at the
  chosen commit with the plain name (or a copy of the dev binary), never by the per-commit flow's
  install.

**Single-name variant**: a repo striving to release makes the package name the binary's name, plain
`<name>` on `main` only:

- **The opening renames**: its bump sets `<name>-dev` beside the suffixed version, and every rung
  and the closing build under the dev name, the closing over the bare version.
- **Land restores**: the rename back to `<name>` is Land's act, so the stable name is only ever
  installed from what `main` will carry.
- **A build script guards the pairing** on every cargo verb: a suffixed version under the stable
  name fails the build, so no mid-cycle install can clobber the consumers' binary.

## Unique per commit (preference, not requirement)

Our general notion is that the version-of-record should change on **every commit**, so a built or
running artifact identifies the exact commit it came from.

- This is a preference, **not** a hard requirement. A project following the cycle protocol may bump
  less often: once per cycle, only at release, and so on. Record the choice in [Recording the
  version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record) if it differs.
- It is achievable because the cycle's versions (below) are **pre-assignable**, unlike the git SHA,
  which a commit cannot contain.

## Suffix scheme

The cycle (opening -> commits -> closing, per the [Cycle protocol](../AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol))
encodes each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a
Preparation**.

This is the manifest's own spelling, read by whoever inspects `Cargo.toml` or `-V` output. It is not
a name for a step: a step is identified by its title, and an in-flight ladder rung carries neither a
number nor a version (see [Steps are named, not numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)).
The identifiers below count commits within a phase, and nothing dereferences one.

- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: the commits between
- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)

**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle, with no ladder and no setup commit, skips `-0` and
starts at `-1` (its first commit). A single-step cycle is one commit, the Close-out, and carries the
bare `X.Y.Z` ([Cycle shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that grows a Preparation later adds the `0`
step without renumbering siblings.

Disambiguation:

- `-10`: commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a Preparation.
- `-1.0`: Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final identifier `0`).

**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:

- `X.Y.Z-3.0`: Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle
- `X.Y.Z-3.1`, `X.Y.Z-3.2`: its commits between
- `X.Y.Z-3`: its Close-out
- `X.Y.Z-3.1.0`: Preparation of the `-3.1` sub-sub-cycle

Bump the version-of-record at the start of every step (the per-commit checklist carries the step),
so the manifest always records the commit it will be part of and, per the preference above, every
commit carries a distinct version.

index fc89552af1..885f30bf6f 100644
--- a/Cargo.toml
+++ b/Cargo.toml
@@ -1,6 +1,6 @@

-version = "0.85.10"
+version = "0.85.11-0"
 edition = "2024"
 
 # The package name is the installed binary's name and never
diff --git a/zDOING.md b/zDOING.md
index b695e21327..4411f4685a 100644
--- a/zDOING.md
+++ b/zDOING.md
@@ -19,4 +19,112 @@ ## Continuation notes
 
 ## In Progress
 
-_No cycle currently in progress._
+### feat: vc-x1 land
+
+Picked from `## Todo` as **commit --land lands a closing already made** (agent, 2026-10-25),
+rewritten as a command of its own (wink + agent, 2026-10-26).
+
+#### Problem
+
+`commit --land` lands only the closing it makes, so a cycle whose last commit is already made, a
+closing pushed without `--land` or a single-step commit made with `--no-push`, is landed by
+commands typed: `move-bookmark`, `push`, a `delete-bookmark` for each bookmark, and `install`. Met
+at the Land of **feat: vc-x1 commit takes a revision** and **fix: the fixture builder drives
+commit**, two cycles stacked and landing together.
+
+#### Solution
+
+- `vc-x1 land -s b|p --source <BM|REV> --onto <BM>`: `--onto` fast-forwarded to `--source` and
+  pushed with the agent half as its partner, and `--source`'s bookmark deleted locally and on
+  origin, `--skip local|remote|both` keeping what it names, `--dry-run` saying each step.
+- `--source` resolves as `--closing`'s argument does. `--onto` is any local bookmark at its origin
+  position that is an ancestor of `--source`, so a bushy tree lands anywhere, and one that is not
+  is refused: `land` makes no merge.
+- `--delete-intermediate-bookmarks` deletes the bookmarks on the commits strictly between, locally
+  and on origin. Without it they are named as merged and kept.
+- `commit --closing ... --land` lands through `land`, one code path.
+
+#### Acceptance check
+
+This series lands by `land` itself, from the work-repo with the closing at `@-`:
+
+```
+vc-x1-dev land -s b --source feat-vc-x1-land --onto main --delete-intermediate-bookmarks --dry-run
+vc-x1-dev land -s b --source feat-vc-x1-land --onto main --delete-intermediate-bookmarks
+vc-x1 install
+```
+
+The dry run lists the fast-forward and the three bookmarks it would delete,
+`feat-vc-x1-commit-takes-a-revision`, `fix-the-fixture-builder-drives-commit`, and
+`feat-vc-x1-land`. Afterwards `main` is at the closing in both repos and on origin, the three
+bookmarks are gone locally and on origin, and `cargo test` passes with a test per rule.
+
+#### Deliberation
+
+- A command of its own: `land`, not `commit --land` with nothing to commit, wink's call
+  (2026-10-26).
+  - The commit is already made, so `commit` names the wrong act, and Land is the agent-files' word
+    for this sequence.
+  - `commit --closing ... --land` stays, as `commit` then `land`.
+- `--source` and `--onto`, both required, named rather than positional (wink, 2026-10-26).
+  - `--onto` over `--dest` and `--trunk`: `--trunk` assumes one line, and a bushy tree lands
+    anywhere.
+  - Named, as `merge` and `move-bookmark` name theirs: no write command takes two positionals, and

## In Progress

### feat: push, commit, and squash-push take flags only

Picked from `## Todo` as **push takes a revision, and the remote's name for it** (wink + agent,
2026-10-24), widened at its planning to every argument a flag (wink + agent, 2026-10-27), and split
in two: this cycle the three commands that publish, the rest **feat: the other commands take flags
only**.

#### Problem

`push`'s positional is a bookmark, so `push -s b @-` is refused, though git needs only a name on
the remote: `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<name>` publishes any commit under a new name, and `jj
git push --named <name>=<REV>` does the same and creates the local bookmark that tracks it. Filed
from the live testing of **feat: vc-x1 closing and land**, whose `[9]` made the refusal say to
leave the revision out.

A positional means something different from command to command: a bookmark to `push` and
`squash-push`, a revision to `commit` and the read commands. So `push -s b feature` has two
readings, the bookmark to move or the commit it is at, and `push` takes its bookmark both as the
positional and as `--bookmark`, one value under two spellings.

#### Solution

- Every argument is a flag, the command names aside, and this cycle does `push`, `commit`, and
  `squash-push`.
- `push -s b|w|a|p [-r REV] [--bookmark NAME]`:
  - REV is the commit to publish, `@-` by default. At `@-` it is the pair's path, unchanged.
    Elsewhere a name alone is published, no pair, today's off-line case, the working copy and the
    root refused.
  - NAME is the remote's name for it, the bookmark at or nearest below REV by default. With no
    bookmark there NAME is required, created at REV and pushed tracked, as `--named` does.
  - A REV that resolves to more than one commit is refused with the count.
- `commit -r REV`, `@` by default, its `--bookmark` unchanged.
- `squash-push --bookmark NAME`.
- An old positional is kept hidden and refused with the flag that replaces it: `push -s b @-`
  names `-r @-`, and `push -s b feature` with `feature` a bookmark names `--bookmark feature`.
- The README's sections for the three, and the agent-files' invocations of them.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a test per rule: `push -r` publishes the commit named, `push --bookmark`
with a new name creates it tracked on origin, a REV of several commits is refused, and each
command's old positional is refused naming its flag. Live, from the rung after push's on: `vc-x1-dev
push -s b @-` fails naming `-r @-`, and a rung committed with `--no-push` is published by
`vc-x1-dev push -s b -r @-`.

#### Deliberation

- Flags only, the command names aside, wink's call (2026-10-27).
  - A positional's meaning differs by command, so the same word reads two ways, and a flag has one
    reading on every command, the reason [Scope is a flag on every command, and push resolves its
    own bookmarks](TODO.md#scope-is-a-flag-on-every-command-and-push-resolves-its-own-bookmarks)
    gave for `-s`, and `land`'s for naming `--source` and `--onto`.
  - jj splits the two the same way: a bookmark name is a revision symbol, and a command that moves
    a bookmark takes its name apart from the revision, `jj bookmark set NAME -r REV` and `jj git
    push --named NAME=REV`.
  - The command line is what the user approves, and a flag says what each word is.
  - `run` and `run-dev` keep their trailing arguments, which are the built binary's.
- `-r, --revision` and `--bookmark`: the names the read commands, `lookup`, and `commit` already
  use, and jj's.
- An old positional is refused, not dropped, wink's call (2026-10-27): a hidden argument whose error
  names the flag, so a stale doc or a habit is told its own fix.
- Two cycles, wink's call (2026-10-27): this one the three commands that publish, which every rung
  runs and the push Todo is about, and the rest in **feat: the other commands take flags only**.
- A REV other than `@-` publishes a name alone, provisional: the pair's checks, the trailer, the
  partner, and the restamp, assume `@-`, and a pair's commit below `@-` was published by its own
  rung.
- The README states the rule in the other cycle, once it holds for every command.

#### Ladder

- [feat: push, commit, and squash-push take flags only opening][f0] (current)
- [feat: push takes --revision and --bookmark][f1]
- [feat: commit and squash-push take flags only][f2]
- [docs: the agent-files name the flags][f3]
- [feat: push, commit, and squash-push take flags only closing][f4]

### feat: push, commit, and squash-push take flags only

Picked from `## Todo` as **push takes a revision, and the remote's name for it** (wink + agent,
2026-10-24), widened at its planning to every argument a flag (wink + agent, 2026-10-27), and split
in two: this cycle the three commands that publish, the rest **feat: the other commands take flags
only**.

#### Problem

`push`'s positional is a bookmark, so `push -s b @-` is refused, though git needs only a name on
the remote: `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<name>` publishes any commit under a new name, and `jj
git push --named <name>=<REV>` does the same and creates the local bookmark that tracks it. Filed
from the live testing of **feat: vc-x1 closing and land**, whose `[9]` made the refusal say to
leave the revision out.

A positional means something different from command to command: a bookmark to `push` and
`squash-push`, a revision to `commit` and the read commands. So `push -s b feature` has two
readings, the bookmark to move or the commit it is at, and `push` takes its bookmark both as the
positional and as `--bookmark`, one value under two spellings.

#### Solution

- Every argument is a flag, the command names aside, and this cycle does `push`, `commit`, and
  `squash-push`.
- `push -s b|w|a|p [-r REV] [--bookmark NAME]`:
  - REV is the commit to publish, `@-` by default. At `@-` it is the pair's path, unchanged.
    Elsewhere a name alone is published, no pair, today's off-line case, the working copy and the
    root refused.
  - NAME is the remote's name for it, the bookmark at or nearest below REV by default. With no
    bookmark there NAME is required, created at REV and pushed tracked, as `--named` does.
  - A REV that resolves to more than one commit is refused with the count.
- `commit -r REV`, `@` by default, its `--bookmark` unchanged.
- `squash-push --bookmark NAME`.
- An old positional is kept hidden and refused with the flag that replaces it: `push -s b @-`
  names `-r @-`, and `push -s b feature` with `feature` a bookmark names `--bookmark feature`.
- The README's sections for the three, and the agent-files' invocations of them.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a test per rule: `push -r` publishes the commit named, `push --bookmark`
with a new name creates it tracked on origin, a REV of several commits is refused, and each
command's old positional is refused naming its flag. Live, from the rung after push's on: `vc-x1-dev
push -s b @-` fails naming `-r @-`, and a rung committed with `--no-push` is published by
`vc-x1-dev push -s b -r @-`.

#### Deliberation

- Flags only, the command names aside, wink's call (2026-10-27).
  - A positional's meaning differs by command, so the same word reads two ways, and a flag has one
    reading on every command, the reason [Scope is a flag on every command, and push resolves its
    own bookmarks](TODO.md#scope-is-a-flag-on-every-command-and-push-resolves-its-own-bookmarks)
    gave for `-s`, and `land`'s for naming `--source` and `--onto`.
  - jj splits the two the same way: a bookmark name is a revision symbol, and a command that moves
    a bookmark takes its name apart from the revision, `jj bookmark set NAME -r REV` and `jj git
    push --named NAME=REV`.
  - The command line is what the user approves, and a flag says what each word is.
  - `run` and `run-dev` keep their trailing arguments, which are the built binary's.
- `-r, --revision` and `--bookmark`: the names the read commands, `lookup`, and `commit` already
  use, and jj's.
- An old positional is refused, not dropped, wink's call (2026-10-27): a hidden argument whose error
  names the flag, so a stale doc or a habit is told its own fix.
- Two cycles, wink's call (2026-10-27): this one the three commands that publish, which every rung
  runs and the push Todo is about, and the rest in **feat: the other commands take flags only**.
- A REV other than `@-` publishes a name alone, provisional: the pair's checks, the trailer, the
  partner, and the restamp, assume `@-`, and a pair's commit below `@-` was published by its own

### feat: push, commit, and squash-push take flags only

Picked from `## Todo` as **push takes a revision, and the remote's name for it** (wink + agent,
2026-10-24), widened at its planning to every argument a flag (wink + agent, 2026-10-27), and split
in two: this cycle the three commands that publish, the rest **feat: the other commands take flags
only**.

#### Problem

`push`'s positional is a bookmark, so `push -s b @-` is refused, though git needs only a name on
the remote: `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<name>` publishes any commit under a new name, and `jj
git push --named <name>=<REV>` does the same and creates the local bookmark that tracks it. Filed
from the live testing of **feat: vc-x1 closing and land**, whose `[9]` made the refusal say to
leave the revision out.

A positional means something different from command to command: a bookmark to `push` and
`squash-push`, a revision to `commit` and the read commands. So `push -s b feature` has two
readings, the bookmark to move or the commit it is at, and `push` takes its bookmark both as the
positional and as `--bookmark`, one value under two spellings.

#### Solution

- Every argument is a flag, the command names aside, and this cycle does `push`, `commit`, and
  `squash-push`.
- `push -s b|w|a|p [-r REV] [--bookmark NAME]`:
  - REV is the commit to publish, `@-` by default. At `@-` it is the pair's path, unchanged.
    Elsewhere a name alone is published, no pair, today's off-line case, the working copy and the
    root refused.
  - NAME is the remote's name for it, the bookmark at or nearest below REV by default. With no
    bookmark there NAME is required, created at REV and pushed tracked, as `--named` does.
  - A REV that resolves to more than one commit is refused with the count.
- `commit -r REV`, `@` by default, its `--bookmark` unchanged.
- `squash-push --bookmark NAME`.
- An old positional is kept hidden and refused with the flag that replaces it: `push -s b @-`
  names `-r @-`, and `push -s b feature` with `feature` a bookmark names `--bookmark feature`.
- The README's sections for the three, and the agent-files' invocations of them.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a test per rule: `push -r` publishes the commit named, `push --bookmark`
with a new name creates it tracked on origin, a REV of several commits is refused, and each
command's old positional is refused naming its flag. Live, from the rung after push's on: `vc-x1-dev
push -s b @-` fails naming `-r @-`, and a rung committed with `--no-push` is published by
`vc-x1-dev push -s b -r @-`.

#### Deliberation

- Flags only, the command names aside, wink's call (2026-10-27).
  - A positional's meaning differs by command, so the same word reads two ways, and a flag has one
    reading on every command, the reason [Scope is a flag on every command, and push resolves its
    own bookmarks](TODO.md#scope-is-a-flag-on-every-command-and-push-resolves-its-own-bookmarks)
    gave for `-s`, and `land`'s for naming `--source` and `--onto`.
  - jj splits the two the same way: a bookmark name is a revision symbol, and a command that moves
    a bookmark takes its name apart from the revision, `jj bookmark set NAME -r REV` and `jj git
    push --named NAME=REV`.
  - The command line is what the user approves, and a flag says what each word is.
  - `run` and `run-dev` keep their trailing arguments, which are the built binary's.
- `-r, --revision` and `--bookmark`: the names the read commands, `lookup`, and `commit` already
  use, and jj's.
- An old positional is refused, not dropped, wink's call (2026-10-27): a hidden argument whose error
  names the flag, so a stale doc or a habit is told its own fix.
- Two cycles, wink's call (2026-10-27): this one the three commands that publish, which every rung
  runs and the push Todo is about, and the rest in **feat: the other commands take flags only**.
- A REV other than `@-` publishes a name alone, provisional: the pair's checks, the trailer, the
  partner, and the restamp, assume `@-`, and a pair's commit below `@-` was published by its own
  rung.
- The README states the rule in the other cycle, once it holds for every command.

### feat: push, commit, and squash-push take flags only

Picked from `## Todo` as **push takes a revision, and the remote's name for it** (wink + agent,
2026-10-24), widened at its planning to every argument a flag (wink + agent, 2026-10-27), and split
in two: this cycle the three commands that publish, the rest **feat: the other commands take flags
only**.

#### Problem

`push`'s positional is a bookmark, so `push -s b @-` is refused, though git needs only a name on
the remote: `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<name>` publishes any commit under a new name, and `jj
git push --named <name>=<REV>` does the same and creates the local bookmark that tracks it. Filed
from the live testing of **feat: vc-x1 closing and land**, whose `[9]` made the refusal say to
leave the revision out.

A positional means something different from command to command: a bookmark to `push` and
`squash-push`, a revision to `commit` and the read commands. So `push -s b feature` has two
readings, the bookmark to move or the commit it is at, and `push` takes its bookmark both as the
positional and as `--bookmark`, one value under two spellings.

#### Solution

- Every argument is a flag, the command names aside, and this cycle does `push`, `commit`, and
  `squash-push`.
- `push -s b|w|a|p [-r REV] [--bookmark NAME]`:
  - REV is the commit to publish, `@-` by default. At `@-` it is the pair's path, unchanged.
    Elsewhere a name alone is published, no pair, today's off-line case, the working copy and the
    root refused.
  - NAME is the remote's name for it, the bookmark at or nearest below REV by default. With no
    bookmark there NAME is required, created at REV and pushed tracked, as `--named` does.
  - A REV that resolves to more than one commit is refused with the count.
- `commit -r REV`, `@` by default, its `--bookmark` unchanged.
- `squash-push --bookmark NAME`.
- An old positional is kept hidden and refused with the flag that replaces it: `push -s b @-`
  names `-r @-`, and `push -s b feature` with `feature` a bookmark names `--bookmark feature`.
- The README's sections for the three, and the agent-files' invocations of them.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a test per rule: `push -r` publishes the commit named, `push --bookmark`
with a new name creates it tracked on origin, a REV of several commits is refused, and each
command's old positional is refused naming its flag. Live, from the rung after push's on: `vc-x1-dev
push -s b @-` fails naming `-r @-`, and a rung committed with `--no-push` is published by
`vc-x1-dev push -s b -r @-`.

#### Deliberation

- Flags only, the command names aside, wink's call (2026-10-27).
  - A positional's meaning differs by command, so the same word reads two ways, and a flag has one
    reading on every command, the reason [Scope is a flag on every command, and push resolves its
    own bookmarks](TODO.md#scope-is-a-flag-on-every-command-and-push-resolves-its-own-bookmarks)
    gave for `-s`, and `land`'s for naming `--source` and `--onto`.
  - jj splits the two the same way: a bookmark name is a revision symbol, and a command that moves
    a bookmark takes its name apart from the revision, `jj bookmark set NAME -r REV` and `jj git
    push --named NAME=REV`.
  - The command line is what the user approves, and a flag says what each word is.
  - `run` keeps its trailing arguments, which are the built binary's.
- `-r, --revision` and `--bookmark`: the names the read commands, `lookup`, and `commit` already
  use, and jj's.
- An old positional is refused, not dropped, wink's call (2026-10-27): a hidden argument whose error
  names the flag, so a stale doc or a habit is told its own fix.
- Two cycles, wink's call (2026-10-27): this one the three commands that publish, which every rung
  runs and the push Todo is about, and the rest in **feat: the other commands take flags only**,
  with **build, install, and run take --dev** folded into it, which keeps `install-dev`, run at
  every rung here, unchanged until this cycle lands.
- A REV other than `@-` publishes a name alone, provisional: the pair's checks, the trailer, the
  partner, and the restamp, assume `@-`, and a pair's commit below `@-` was published by its own
  rung.
- The README states the rule in the other cycle, once it holds for every command.

# Commit model

Two commit bodies from the `config loader` cycle in [cycle-model.md](cycle-model.md), shown as
specimens rather than a skeleton: a work rung's body and a bookend's. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [Commit-body form](prose.md#commit-body-form).

## A work rung

Title: `refactor: split loader from parser`

```
Config loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load a
config without parsing it and a test cannot parse one without a file on
disk. The move into its own module is what forces the split.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config::loader` finds and reads the file and returns the text with
    its path, so a caller that only wants to know which file was read
    stops there.
  - `config::parser` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands
    it a string and never touches the filesystem.
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field
    access moves behind the module boundary and the CLI no longer knows
    the file's shape.
```

The intro states this commit's problem and defines "split", the word the title assumes. Each `*`
is one facet of it, each `-` under a `*` answers that facet, and nothing names a file that the
diff already lists.

## A bookend

Title: `refactor: extract config loader opening`

```
Opens the cycle "refactor: extract config loader". Its record is the
In Progress block in TODO.md.
```

A bookend resolves no problem of its own, so its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the
cycle by its title and pointing at its record. The closing's body is the same shape with "Closes".

132	### Commit-body form
133	
134	The specimen is [commit-model.md](commit-model.md). A commit body is the [Problem-first
135	shape](#problem-first-shape) with one addition: a body whose
136	problem has several sub-problems arranges them by a fixed recursion, so a reader knows what any
137	bullet is from its marker and its depth. The earlier statement, "a problem statement then a solution
138	statement, both broad", left that arrangement to taste, and taste converged slowly and separately.
139	
140	- **An intro paragraph states the general problem**, and defines any word the title assumes. It is
141	  mandatory. [Prose form](#prose-form) wants it regardless, and a body opening on a bullet is a body
142	  a `--body` flag can mistake for an option. The problem is *this commit's*, never the cycle's: the
143	  cycle's problem lives in the In Progress block, and a body whose problems outnumber what the diff
144	  resolves is describing something larger than the commit.
145	- **`*` bullets are the problem's facets**: sub-problems that decompose the intro's general problem,
146	  not a grab-bag of unrelated fixes. A body reaching for unrelated problem bullets is usually asking
147	  to be more than one commit.
148	- **`-` bullets are solutions**, and every `-` sits under a `*`, solving that facet. A `-` with no
149	  `*` above it reads as a solution to nothing, so there are no top-level solutions: a solution that
150	  retires every facet at once is written under each, or the facets are one.
151	- **One facet is the trivial commit**: the intro, one `*`, one or more `-` under it. Not a second
152	  form, the general form at its smallest.
153	- **A bookend body is a pointer**: an opening or closing commit resolves no problem of its own, so
154	  its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the cycle by its title and pointing at its record,
155	  the In Progress block. No `*`, no `-`.
156	
157	**The markers are typed on purpose**: `*` always means problem, `-` always means solution, and the
158	pairing is what a reader counts on: the `-` answers the `*` above it, with no rule to consult. The
159	typing also keeps history greppable (`^\* ` finds every facet, `^ - ` every solution). Bodies are
160	read as plain text, in `jj log` and in terminals, where the markers survive, and if a renderer ever
161	flattens them the indentation still carries the structure. So the mixed markers are deliberate, and
162	a linter's consistent-marker rule is wrong to normalize them.
163	
164	Unchanged by this: no version in title or body, no file list, no deliberation, titles per
165	[Conventional-commit shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit).

shape](#problem-first-shape) with one addition: a body whose
problem has several sub-problems arranges them by a fixed recursion, so a reader knows what any
bullet is from its marker and its depth. The earlier statement, "a problem statement then a solution
statement, both broad", left that arrangement to taste, and taste converged slowly and separately.

- **An intro paragraph states the general problem**, and defines any word the title assumes. It is

  not a grab-bag of unrelated fixes. A body reaching for unrelated problem bullets is usually asking
  to be more than one commit.
- **`-` bullets are solutions**, and every `-` sits under a `*`, solving that facet. A `-` with no

  retires every facet at once is written under each, or the facets are one.

record's home, and the cycle that makes this file the rule is [The cycle-record moves out of
TODO.md into zDOING.md](TODO.md#the-cycle-record-moves-out-of-todomd-into-zdoingmd).

## Continuation notes

Where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a record: read first, acted
on, and reset to `_None._` by the reader. Kept here by the trial and no longer in `TODO.md`,
where [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint) still says to look.

## In Progress

### feat: push, commit, and squash-push take flags only

Picked from `## Todo` as **push takes a revision, and the remote's name for it** (wink + agent,
2026-10-24), widened at its planning to every argument a flag (wink + agent, 2026-10-27), and split
in two: this cycle the three commands that publish, the rest **feat: the other commands take flags
only**.

#### Problem

`push`'s positional is a bookmark, so `push -s b @-` is refused, though git needs only a name on
the remote: `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<name>` publishes any commit under a new name, and `jj
git push --named <name>=<REV>` does the same and creates the local bookmark that tracks it. Filed
from the live testing of **feat: vc-x1 closing and land**, whose `[9]` made the refusal say to
leave the revision out.

A positional means something different from command to command: a bookmark to `push` and
`squash-push`, a revision to `commit` and the read commands. So `push -s b feature` has two
readings, the bookmark to move or the commit it is at, and `push` takes its bookmark both as the
positional and as `--bookmark`, one value under two spellings.

#### Solution

- Every argument is a flag, the command names aside, and this cycle does `push`, `commit`, and
  `squash-push`.
- `push -s b|w|a|p [-r REV] [--bookmark NAME]`:
  - REV is the commit to publish, `@-` by default. At `@-` it is the pair's path, unchanged.
    Elsewhere a name alone is published, no pair, today's off-line case, the working copy and the
    root refused.
  - NAME is the remote's name for it, the bookmark at or nearest below REV by default. With no
    bookmark there NAME is required, created at REV and pushed tracked, as `--named` does.
  - A REV that resolves to more than one commit is refused with the count.
- `commit -r REV`, `@` by default, its `--bookmark` unchanged.
- `squash-push --bookmark NAME`.
- An old positional is kept hidden and refused with the flag that replaces it: `push -s b @-`
  names `-r @-`, and `push -s b feature` with `feature` a bookmark names `--bookmark feature`.
- The README's sections for the three, and the agent-files' invocations of them.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a test per rule: `push -r` publishes the commit named, `push --bookmark`
with a new name creates it tracked on origin, a REV of several commits is refused, and each
command's old positional is refused naming its flag. Live, from the rung after push's on: `vc-x1-dev
push -s b @-` fails naming `-r @-`, and a rung committed with `--no-push` is published by
`vc-x1-dev push -s b -r @-`.

#### Deliberation

- Flags only, the command names aside, wink's call (2026-10-27).
  - A positional's meaning differs by command, so the same word reads two ways, and a flag has one
    reading on every command, the reason [Scope is a flag on every command, and push resolves its
    own bookmarks](TODO.md#scope-is-a-flag-on-every-command-and-push-resolves-its-own-bookmarks)
    gave for `-s`, and `land`'s for naming `--source` and `--onto`.
  - jj splits the two the same way: a bookmark name is a revision symbol, and a command that moves
    a bookmark takes its name apart from the revision, `jj bookmark set NAME -r REV` and `jj git
    push --named NAME=REV`.
  - The command line is what the user approves, and a flag says what each word is.
  - `run` keeps its trailing arguments, which are the built binary's.
- `-r, --revision` and `--bookmark`: the names the read commands, `lookup`, and `commit` already
  use, and jj's.
- An old positional is refused, not dropped, wink's call (2026-10-27): a hidden argument whose error

Picked from `## Todo` as **push takes a revision, and the remote's name for it** (wink + agent,
2026-10-24), widened at its planning to every argument a flag (wink + agent, 2026-10-27), and split
in two: this cycle the three commands that publish, the rest **feat: the other commands take flags
only**.

#### Problem

`push`'s positional is a bookmark, so `push -s b @-` is refused, though git needs only a name on
the remote: `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<name>` publishes any commit under a new name, and `jj
git push --named <name>=<REV>` does the same and creates the local bookmark that tracks it. Filed
from the live testing of **feat: vc-x1 closing and land**, whose `[9]` made the refusal say to
leave the revision out.

A positional means something different from command to command: a bookmark to `push` and
`squash-push`, a revision to `commit` and the read commands. So `push -s b feature` has two
readings, the bookmark to move or the commit it is at, and `push` takes its bookmark both as the
positional and as `--bookmark`, one value under two spellings.

#### Solution

- Every argument is a flag, the command names aside, and this cycle does `push`, `commit`, and
  `squash-push`.
- `push -s b|w|a|p [-r REV] [--bookmark NAME]`:
  - REV is the commit to publish, `@-` by default. At `@-` it is the pair's path, unchanged.
    Elsewhere a name alone is published, no pair, today's off-line case, the working copy and the
    root refused.
  - NAME is the remote's name for it, the bookmark at or nearest below REV by default. With no
    bookmark there NAME is required, created at REV and pushed tracked, as `--named` does.
  - A REV that resolves to more than one commit is refused with the count.
- `commit -r REV`, `@` by default, its `--bookmark` unchanged.
- `squash-push --bookmark NAME`.
- An old positional is kept hidden and refused with the flag that replaces it: `push -s b @-`
  names `-r @-`, and `push -s b feature` with `feature` a bookmark names `--bookmark feature`.
- The README's sections for the three, and the agent-files' invocations of them.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a test per rule: `push -r` publishes the commit named, `push --bookmark`
with a new name creates it tracked on origin, a REV of several commits is refused, and each
command's old positional is refused naming its flag. Live, from the rung after push's on: `vc-x1-dev
push -s b @-` fails naming `-r @-`, and a rung committed with `--no-push` is published by
`vc-x1-dev push -s b -r @-`.

#### Deliberation

- Flags only, the command names aside, wink's call (2026-10-27).
  - A positional's meaning differs by command, so the same word reads two ways, and a flag has one
    reading on every command, the reason [Scope is a flag on every command, and push resolves its
    own bookmarks](TODO.md#scope-is-a-flag-on-every-command-and-push-resolves-its-own-bookmarks)
    gave for `-s`, and `land`'s for naming `--source` and `--onto`.
  - jj splits the two the same way: a bookmark name is a revision symbol, and a command that moves
    a bookmark takes its name apart from the revision, `jj bookmark set NAME -r REV` and `jj git
    push --named NAME=REV`.
  - The command line is what the user approves, and a flag says what each word is.
  - `run` keeps its trailing arguments, which are the built binary's.
- `-r, --revision` and `--bookmark`: the names the read commands, `lookup`, and `commit` already
  use, and jj's.
- An old positional is refused, not dropped, wink's call (2026-10-27): a hidden argument whose error

# `vc-x1-dev` instead, guarded by build.rs (chores-16, 0.78.3).

[lints.clippy]
# The process-spawn ban: `Command::new` is disallowed via
# clippy.toml's `disallowed-methods`, and deny (not warn) so a bare
# new spawn site fails `cargo clippy` even without `-D warnings`.
# The documented allowlist lives in clippy.toml.
disallowed_methods = "deny"

[dependencies]
chrono = { version = "0.4", default-features = false, features = ["now"] }
clap = { version = "4.6", features = ["derive", "wrap_help"] }
clap_complete = { version = "4.6", features = ["unstable-dynamic"] }
futures = "0.3"
# The gix jj-lib 0.46 resolves (no features of our own): the
# session's lock-contention downcast needs type identity with the
# errors jj-lib returns, and init's bare-repo creation reuses it.
gix = { version = "0.88", default-features = false }
# When raising jj-lib: check whether it now offers the commits a
# remote's bookmarks are on without fetching. If so, `git_command`
# in src/jj/session.rs and its two callers take it, and
# clippy.toml's register entry 6 closes (TODO.md > ## Waiting).
jj-lib = "0.46"
log = { version = "0.4", features = ["std"] }
pollster = "1.0"
# The rng jj-lib's `SecureConfig` takes to mint a repo's config id,
# at jj-lib 0.46's versions so the types are its own, seeded the way
# jj-cli seeds it (src/jj/session.rs `load_repo_config`).
rand = "0.10"
rand_chacha = "0.10"
serde_json = "1"

[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]
libc = "0.2"

### push

Publish a rung's pair, or a bookmark on a commit already made. Push carries no description and
writes none, so what was reviewed is what goes out: `commit` makes the pair and pushes it unless
told not to, and push publishes one it kept local, completing the agent half as its partner. A
named bookmark off the line `@-` is on, on a commit already made, is published where it is, a name
and no pair: a bookmark on the working copy is refused, since `commit` is what turns it into a
commit, and one on the root has nothing to publish.

```bash
vc-x1 push -s b                  # the pair, on the bookmark the work @- sits on
vc-x1 push -s b feature          # the same, the bookmark named as a check
vc-x1 push -s b side             # a bookmark off the line, on a commit made, published where it is
vc-x1 push -s w                  # the work half only
vc-x1 push -s a                  # the agent half only, the remainder of a run that stopped
vc-x1 push -s p -R ../other      # a plain repo's @- on its bookmark, no trailer asked for
vc-x1 push -s b --dry-run        # plan and print, move nothing
```

Push publishes the work `@-`, so new work in `@`, the next rung started, is left as it is, and
push says so. What push refuses, with both repos as they were:

- a work `@-` with no `ochid:` trailer: not a pair's commit, so `commit` makes one first
- two bookmarks on the line and none named, or a named bookmark on the working copy or the root

The two halves are independent, since each trailer is fixed before push runs, so `push -s b` is
`push -s a` then `push -s w`, the order the pair is completed in:

| Half | What it does |
|------|--------------|
| agent | Complete the partner by the state found: the agent `@-` names the work commit (`commit -s b`), so the journal folds into it; or the agent `@` is the change the work commit names (`commit -s w`), or the agent repo changed since, so the journal is committed as the partner with the work commit's own text. Then squash-push `main` (see [squash-push](#squash-push)) |
| work | Check the work trailer names the partner, restamping the unpublished work commit when it does not, said out loud. Then `jj bookmark set <bookmark> -r @-`, verify its remote refs are tracked, and `jj git push --bookmark <bookmark>` |

**Rerunning is always safe.** There is no saved state and no resume: every stage checks its own
precondition and does nothing when its work is already done, so re-running after a failure is simply
running. If a run fails, push stops and reports. A half that fails before its own push restores the
repo it touched via `jj op restore` to a snapshot taken moments earlier in the same process. Once a
half's push succeeds that half is published: from there a change is either a new pair on top, or an
amend of what was pushed, where [`squash-push`](#squash-push) folds the working copy into the last
commit and force-updates the remote. See the protocol's
[at-rest contract](AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push).

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `-s, --scope <SCOPE>` | Required: `b|both` the pair, `w|work` the work half, `a|agent` the agent half, `p|por` a plain repo |
| `-R, --repo <PATH>` | Where: a path in the workspace, or the plain repo [default: the cwd] |
| `[BOOKMARK]` | Work-repo bookmark to advance, a check against the line `@-` is on [default: that line's bookmark], the positional form of `--bookmark` |
| `--bookmark <NAME>` | Same as positional (mutually exclusive) |
| `--dry-run` | Plan and print what would run, no side effects |
| `--step` | Pause after every stage for an extra continue-prompt |
| `-y, --yes` | Pass the `--step` gates without asking |

See [Add push subcommand (0.37.0)](./notes/chores/chores-05.md#add-push-subcommand-0370) for the
full design and [per-step record](./notes/chores/chores-05.md#per-step-record) for what each
`0.37.0-N` dev step shipped.

  where it was moved sideways before.

### feat: push, commit, and squash-push take flags only

Picked from `## Todo` as **push takes a revision, and the remote's name for it** (wink + agent,
2026-10-24), widened at its planning to every argument a flag (wink + agent, 2026-10-27), and split
in two: this cycle the three commands that publish, the rest **feat: the other commands take flags
only**.

#### Problem

`push`'s positional is a bookmark, so `push -s b @-` is refused, though git needs only a name on
the remote: `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<name>` publishes any commit under a new name, and `jj
git push --named <name>=<REV>` does the same and creates the local bookmark that tracks it. Filed
from the live testing of **feat: vc-x1 closing and land**, whose `[9]` made the refusal say to
leave the revision out.

A positional means something different from command to command: a bookmark to `push` and
`squash-push`, a revision to `commit` and the read commands. So `push -s b feature` has two
readings, the bookmark to move or the commit it is at, and `push` takes its bookmark both as the
positional and as `--bookmark`, one value under two spellings.

#### Solution

- Every argument is a flag, the command names aside, and this cycle does `push`, `commit`, and
  `squash-push`.
- `push -s b|w|a|p [-r REV] [--bookmark NAME]`:
  - REV is the commit to publish, `@-` by default. At `@-` it is the pair's path, unchanged.
    Elsewhere a name alone is published, no pair, today's off-line case, the working copy and the
    root refused.
  - NAME is the remote's name for it, the bookmark at or nearest below REV by default. With no
    bookmark there NAME is required, created at REV and pushed tracked, as `--named` does.
  - A REV that resolves to more than one commit is refused with the count.
- `commit -r REV`, `@` by default, its `--bookmark` unchanged.
- `squash-push --bookmark NAME`.
- An old positional is kept hidden and refused with the flag that replaces it: `push -s b @-`
  names `-r @-`, and `push -s b feature` with `feature` a bookmark names `--bookmark feature`.
- The README's sections for the three, and the agent-files' invocations of them.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a test per rule: `push -r` publishes the commit named, `push --bookmark`
with a new name creates it tracked on origin, a REV of several commits is refused, and each
command's old positional is refused naming its flag. Live, from the rung after push's on: `vc-x1-dev
push -s b @-` fails naming `-r @-`, and a rung committed with `--no-push` is published by
`vc-x1-dev push -s b -r @-`.

#### Deliberation

- Flags only, the command names aside, wink's call (2026-10-27).
  - A positional's meaning differs by command, so the same word reads two ways, and a flag has one
    reading on every command, the reason [Scope is a flag on every command, and push resolves its
    own bookmarks](TODO.md#scope-is-a-flag-on-every-command-and-push-resolves-its-own-bookmarks)
    gave for `-s`, and `land`'s for naming `--source` and `--onto`.
  - jj splits the two the same way: a bookmark name is a revision symbol, and a command that moves
    a bookmark takes its name apart from the revision, `jj bookmark set NAME -r REV` and `jj git
    push --named NAME=REV`.
  - The command line is what the user approves, and a flag says what each word is.
  - `run` keeps its trailing arguments, which are the built binary's.
- `-r, --revision` and `--bookmark`: the names the read commands, `lookup`, and `commit` already
  use, and jj's.
- An old positional is refused, not dropped, wink's call (2026-10-27): a hidden argument whose error
  names the flag, so a stale doc or a habit is told its own fix.
- Two cycles, wink's call (2026-10-27): this one the three commands that publish, which every rung
  runs and the push Todo is about, and the rest in **feat: the other commands take flags only**,
  with **build, install, and run take --dev** folded into it, which keeps `install-dev`, run at
  every rung here, unchanged until this cycle lands, and **init and clone take --scope por**,
  whose commands it touches.
- A REV other than `@-` publishes a name alone, provisional: the pair's checks, the trailer, the
  partner, and the restamp, assume `@-`, and a pair's commit below `@-` was published by its own
  rung.
- The README states the rule in the other cycle, once it holds for every command.
- Waiver, wink's "Continue and complete this cycle except for landing on main" (2026-10-27), after
  the opening's push.
  - Covers every rung from **feat: push takes --revision and --bookmark** through the closing: the
    work review, the description review, the per-push approval, and the hard stop after each push.
  - Does not cover Land: the closing is pushed without `--land`, and the close-out shape is the
    default, trapezoid, until wink chooses at the Land.
  - Validation still runs before every push.

56	/// commit and publishes it: rewriting an already-pushed commit is
57	/// a forced update. `-s` is required: `squash-push -s a` is the
58	/// agent repo's session tail folded and pushed, `-s w` or `-s b`
59	/// the fold-and-publish that asks nothing, and `-s p` a plain repo.
60	#[derive(Args, Debug)]
61	pub struct SquashPushArgs {
62	    /// Bookmark to advance and push [default: the bookmark of the
63	    /// line you are on, the nearest one at or above the squash
64	    /// target]
65	    #[arg(value_name = "BOOKMARK")]
66	    pub bookmark: Option<String>,
67	
68	    /// Where: a path in the workspace for `-s w|a|b`, its root or
69	    /// either repo, or the repo itself for `-s p` [default: the
70	    /// current directory]

72	    pub repo: Option<PathBuf>,

102	/// Per-invocation squash-push inputs: the clap-free shape the op

104	/// via `TryFrom` (fallible only on repo-path canonicalization),
105	/// while `vc-x1 push`'s `squash-push-bot` stage constructs it
106	/// directly.
107	#[derive(Debug)]
108	pub struct SquashPushParams {
109	    pub repo: PathBuf,
110	    pub squash: SquashSpec,
111	    pub bookmark: String,
112	    /// This run is the user's at-rest invocation rather than
113	    /// `vc-x1 push`'s `squash-push-bot` stage.
114	    ///
115	    /// Everything addressed to a person is gated on it: the
116	    /// publish-mismatch report, the precheck's and after-check's
117	    /// lines, and the prompt. Mid-push every one of them is wrong.
118	    /// The mismatch is the normal state there, since `bookmark-set`
119	    /// just moved the bookmark and this stage is what publishes it.
120	    /// The verdict lines describe a repo caught mid-sequence. And
121	    /// nobody is watching to answer a prompt.
122	    ///

124	    /// nothing to do should still do nothing, which is the behavior
125	    /// the `already sync'd` early return gave push before the
126	    /// precheck replaced it.
127	    pub at_rest: bool,
128	    /// Act without asking once the precheck has found work. True is
129	    /// today's behavior and the built-in default, so the prompt is
130	    /// opt-in. Resolved from `--yes`, then `--ask`, then the repo's
131	    /// `squash-push.yes`, then the built-in.
132	    pub yes: bool,
133	    /// Print what the precheck found and the steps it would take,
134	    /// and change nothing.
135	    pub dry_run: bool,
136	}
137	
138	/// The `yes` choice: the flags, then the config key, then the
139	/// built-in default.
140	///
141	/// The same order `agent-files diff` resolves its `--custom` by. A
142	/// boolean flag cannot turn a configured `true` back off, which is
143	/// why `--ask` exists rather than a `--no-yes`.
144	pub fn resolve_yes(yes: bool, ask: bool, key_value: Option<bool>, default: bool) -> bool {
145	    if yes {
146	        true
147	    } else if ask {
148	        false
149	    } else {
150	        key_value.unwrap_or(default)
151	    }
152	}
153	
154	/// The `squash-push.yes` key of the config in `repo`, if any.
155	///
156	/// Read from the repo the command is pointed at rather than from the
157	/// workspace, so each side may answer differently and a plain repo
158	/// outside a workspace simply has no answer.
159	fn config_yes(repo: &Path) -> Result<Option<bool>, Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
160	    let Some(cfg) = crate::config_md::load(repo)? else {
161	        return Ok(None);
162	    };
163	    match crate::toml_simple::toml_get(&cfg.map, "squash-push.yes").map(String::as_str) {
164	        None => Ok(None),
165	        Some("true") => Ok(Some(true)),
166	        Some("false") => Ok(Some(false)),
167	        Some(other) => Err(format!(
168	            "squash-push.yes: invalid bool {other:?}: expected true or false, unquoted"
169	        )
170	        .into()),
171	    }
172	}
173	
174	/// The params for one resolved repo: the `--squash` default filled
175	/// and BOOKMARK mapped straight over, or read from the repo when
176	/// absent. `repo` is already canonical, the resolver's.
177	fn params_for(a: &SquashPushArgs, repo: PathBuf) -> Result<SquashPushParams, String> {
178	    {
179	        let yes = resolve_yes(
180	            a.yes,
181	            a.ask,
182	            config_yes(&repo).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?,
183	            crate::config_schema::SQUASH_PUSH_YES_DEFAULT,
184	        );
185	        let squash = a.squash.value.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| SquashSpec {
186	            source: "@".to_string(),
187	            target: "@-".to_string(),
188	        }); // OK: --squash absent -> the command's default @,@- pair
189	        let bookmark = match &a.bookmark {
190	            Some(b) => b.clone(),
191	            None => current_bookmark(&repo, &squash.target).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?,
192	        };
193	        Ok(SquashPushParams {
194	            repo,
195	            squash: squash.clone(),
196	            bookmark,
197	            at_rest: true,
198	            yes,
199	            dry_run: a.dry_run.value,
200	        })
201	    }
202	}
203	
204	/// One `SquashPushParams` per repo `-s` and `-R` resolve to, in
205	/// scope order, work before agent.
206	fn params_for_args(a: &SquashPushArgs) -> Result<Vec<SquashPushParams>, String> {
207	    crate::common::resolve_scoped_repos(&a.scope, a.repo.as_deref())
208	        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
209	        .into_iter()
210	        .map(|repo| params_for(a, repo))
211	        .collect()
212	}

Captures a repo's trailing working-copy writes into the last\n\
        commit and publishes it: rewriting an already-pushed commit,\n\
        so the push is a forced update. Built for the bot repo\n\
        (`.claude`, the session tail), and useful on the work repo as\n\
        a deliberate amend-and-push.\n\n\
        Zero-ceremony default: bare `vc-x1 squash-push` squashes\n\
        @ -> @- in `.` and pushes the bookmark of the line you are\n\
        on. With an empty `@` but work still to do, the squash is\n\
        skipped and the push still runs.\n\n\
        BOOKMARK defaults to the line's own bookmark, the nearest one\n\
        at or above the squash target, and there is no literal\n\
        default. On the agent repo that is `main`. On a work repo\n\
        running a cycle it is the topic bookmark, so a bare run\n\
        publishes the line you are working and never advances `main`.\n\
        Several candidates, or none, is an error asking you to name\n\
        one, since a wrong guess here publishes something.\n\n\
        A precheck asks whether the run has work at all: the working\n\
        copy at rest, the bookmark at its origin, and the bookmark\n\
        already at the squash target. That third condition is there\n\
        because a bookmark behind its target has a commit to publish\n\
        even when it matches origin. A run with no work prints\n\
        `<label>: clean` and exits 0 having touched nothing, <label>\n\
        being the repo's directory name. Every other run prints the\n\
        same line after the push, as a report only: the exit code\n\
        says whether the push completed, not what that line found.\n\n\
        With work found, the run acts without asking, the default\n\
        `squash-push.yes` sets. --ask turns the prompt on for one run\n\
        and -y/--yes turns it off. With the prompt on, a non-tty run\n\
        is an error rather than a hang, and declining is an error too.\n\n\
        As `vc-x1 push`'s squash-push-bot stage it says nothing and\n\
        asks nothing, there being no one mid-push to read a line or\n\
        answer a prompt. The precheck's decision still applies, so a\n\
        stage with no work still does nothing."
    )]
    SquashPush(squash_push::SquashPushArgs),

content.content:
Every run begins by asking whether it has work, and ends by saying what it left. A run with nothing
to do prints `<label>: clean` and exits 0 having touched nothing, so the command is safe to call
when you are unsure, and every other run prints that line again after the push. With work found it
acts without asking, which is what `squash-push.yes` defaults to, and `--ask` turns a confirmation
prompt on. The details of each are in the behavior notes below.

```
# The agent repo: squash @ -> @-, advance main, push, from anywhere in the workspace
vc-x1 squash-push -s a

# Both repos, work first: the fold-and-publish that asks nothing
vc-x1 squash-push -s b

# A plain repo with no pair, the current directory's
vc-x1 squash-push -s p

# Name the bookmark explicitly, with a custom squash pair, on the work repo
vc-x1 squash-push feature -s w --squash @,@--

# Confirm before acting, overriding a configured squash-push.yes
vc-x1 squash-push -s a --ask

# Say what it found and what it would do, and change nothing
vc-x1 squash-push -s a --dry-run
```

published-history rewrite, so the push is a forced update.

The primary use case is folding the bot repo's session tail: session data keeps landing in `@` after
the last commit (including the record of the push itself), and only the user, acting after the bot
goes quiet, can capture all of it. Zero ceremony by design:

`BOOKMARK` defaults to the bookmark of the line you are on, the nearest one at or above the squash
target. There is no literal default: on the agent repo the line's bookmark is `main`, and on a work
repo running a cycle it is the topic bookmark, so a bare run publishes the line you are working and
never advances `main`. Several candidates, or none, is an error asking you to name one, since a
wrong guess publishes something. A literal `main` default used to sit here, and on 2026-09-17 a bare
vc-x1: clean

### feat: push, commit, and squash-push take flags only

Picked from `## Todo` as **push takes a revision, and the remote's name for it** (wink + agent,
2026-10-24), widened at its planning to every argument a flag (wink + agent, 2026-10-27), and split
in two: this cycle the three commands that publish, the rest **feat: the other commands take flags
only**.

#### Problem

`push`'s positional is a bookmark, so `push -s b @-` is refused, though git needs only a name on
the remote: `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<name>` publishes any commit under a new name, and `jj
git push --named <name>=<REV>` does the same and creates the local bookmark that tracks it. Filed
from the live testing of **feat: vc-x1 closing and land**, whose `[9]` made the refusal say to
leave the revision out.

A positional means something different from command to command: a bookmark to `push` and
`squash-push`, a revision to `commit` and the read commands. So `push -s b feature` has two
readings, the bookmark to move or the commit it is at, and `push` takes its bookmark both as the
positional and as `--bookmark`, one value under two spellings.

#### Solution

- Every argument is a flag, the command names aside, and this cycle does `push`, `commit`, and
  `squash-push`.
- `push -s b|w|a|p [-r REV] [--bookmark NAME]`:
  - REV is the commit to publish, `@-` by default. At `@-` it is the pair's path, unchanged.
    Elsewhere a name alone is published, no pair, today's off-line case, the working copy and the
    root refused.
  - NAME is the remote's name for it, the bookmark at or nearest below REV by default. With no
    bookmark there NAME is required, created at REV and pushed tracked, as `--named` does.
  - A REV that resolves to more than one commit is refused with the count.
- `commit -r REV`, `@` by default, its `--bookmark` unchanged.
- `squash-push --bookmark NAME`.
- An old positional is kept hidden and refused with the flag that replaces it: `push -s b @-`
  names `-r @-`, and `push -s b feature` with `feature` a bookmark names `--bookmark feature`.
- The README's sections for the three, and the agent-files' invocations of them.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a test per rule: `push -r` publishes the commit named, `push --bookmark`
with a new name creates it tracked on origin, a REV of several commits is refused, and each
command's old positional is refused naming its flag. Live, from the rung after push's on: `vc-x1-dev
push -s b @-` fails naming `-r @-`, and a rung committed with `--no-push` is published by
`vc-x1-dev push -s b -r @-`.

#### Deliberation

- Flags only, the command names aside, wink's call (2026-10-27).
  - A positional's meaning differs by command, so the same word reads two ways, and a flag has one
    reading on every command, the reason [Scope is a flag on every command, and push resolves its
    own bookmarks](TODO.md#scope-is-a-flag-on-every-command-and-push-resolves-its-own-bookmarks)
    gave for `-s`, and `land`'s for naming `--source` and `--onto`.
  - jj splits the two the same way: a bookmark name is a revision symbol, and a command that moves
    a bookmark takes its name apart from the revision, `jj bookmark set NAME -r REV` and `jj git
    push --named NAME=REV`.
  - The command line is what the user approves, and a flag says what each word is.
  - `run` keeps its trailing arguments, which are the built binary's.
- `-r, --revision` and `--bookmark`: the names the read commands, `lookup`, and `commit` already
  use, and jj's.
- An old positional is refused, not dropped, wink's call (2026-10-27): a hidden argument whose error
  names the flag, so a stale doc or a habit is told its own fix.
- Two cycles, wink's call (2026-10-27): this one the three commands that publish, which every rung
  runs and the push Todo is about, and the rest in **feat: the other commands take flags only**,
  with **build, install, and run take --dev** folded into it, which keeps `install-dev`, run at
  every rung here, unchanged until this cycle lands, and **init and clone take --scope por**,
  whose commands it touches.
- A REV other than `@-` publishes a name alone, provisional: the pair's checks, the trailer, the
  partner, and the restamp, assume `@-`, and a pair's commit below `@-` was published by its own
  rung.
- The README states the rule in the other cycle, once it holds for every command.
- Waiver, wink's "Continue and complete this cycle except for landing on main" (2026-10-27), after
  the opening's push.
  - Covers every rung from **feat: push takes --revision and --bookmark** through the closing: the
    work review, the description review, the per-push approval, and the hard stop after each push.
  - Does not cover Land: the closing is pushed without `--land`, and the close-out shape is the
    default, trapezoid, until wink chooses at the Land.
  - Validation still runs before every push.

##### feat: push takes --revision and --bookmark

`push`'s positional goes hidden and refused, `-r` names the commit and `--bookmark` the remote's
name, a new name created tracked, and the refusal helper the other commands reuse.

- `options_flags::retired_positional::refusal`, the one wording every retired positional gets: the
  command, "the positional is retired, every argument is a flag", and the flag form with the value
  in place, so the next two rungs and the other cycle share it.
- `push`'s refusal names `--bookmark` when the value is a local bookmark in the repo `-R` names,
  else `-r`, the lookup made in `to_params` and a failed one only losing the hint.
- Two paths, split on whether REV is the work `@-` by commit id, so `-r @-`, `-r <its chid>`, and
  `-r <its bookmark>` all take the pair's:
  - The pair's path is unchanged but for `--bookmark` taking a new name, set at `@-` by the work
    half's own `bookmark_set` and tracked by its push, the call the opening's bookmark uses.
  - `publish_elsewhere`, which replaces `publish_name`, publishes a name alone: the one bookmark at

- `-r` with `-s a` is refused, and `--bookmark` given a revision names `-r`.

- `tests/cli_sync.rs` called `push -s w main`, and the full validation found it, the one CLI caller

### feat: push, commit, and squash-push take flags only

Picked from `## Todo` as **push takes a revision, and the remote's name for it** (wink + agent,
2026-10-24), widened at its planning to every argument a flag (wink + agent, 2026-10-27), and split
in two: this cycle the three commands that publish, the rest **feat: the other commands take flags
only**.

#### Problem

`push`'s positional is a bookmark, so `push -s b @-` is refused, though git needs only a name on
the remote: `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<name>` publishes any commit under a new name, and `jj
git push --named <name>=<REV>` does the same and creates the local bookmark that tracks it. Filed
from the live testing of **feat: vc-x1 closing and land**, whose `[9]` made the refusal say to
leave the revision out.

A positional means something different from command to command: a bookmark to `push` and
`squash-push`, a revision to `commit` and the read commands. So `push -s b feature` has two
readings, the bookmark to move or the commit it is at, and `push` takes its bookmark both as the
positional and as `--bookmark`, one value under two spellings.

#### Solution

- Every argument is a flag, the command names aside, and this cycle does `push`, `commit`, and
  `squash-push`.
- `push -s b|w|a|p [-r REV] [--bookmark NAME]`:
  - REV is the commit to publish, `@-` by default. At `@-` it is the pair's path, unchanged.
    Elsewhere a name alone is published, no pair, today's off-line case, the working copy and the
    root refused.
  - NAME is the remote's name for it, the bookmark at or nearest below REV by default. With no
    bookmark there NAME is required, created at REV and pushed tracked, as `--named` does.
  - A REV that resolves to more than one commit is refused with the count.
- `commit -r REV`, `@` by default, its `--bookmark` unchanged.
- `squash-push --bookmark NAME`.
- An old positional is kept hidden and refused with the flag that replaces it: `push -s b @-`
  names `-r @-`, and `push -s b feature` with `feature` a bookmark names `--bookmark feature`.
- The README's sections for the three, and the agent-files' invocations of them.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a test per rule: `push -r` publishes the commit named, `push --bookmark`
with a new name creates it tracked on origin, a REV of several commits is refused, and each
command's old positional is refused naming its flag. Live, from the rung after push's on: `vc-x1-dev
push -s b @-` fails naming `-r @-`, and a rung committed with `--no-push` is published by
`vc-x1-dev push -s b -r @-`.

#### Deliberation

- Flags only, the command names aside, wink's call (2026-10-27).
  - A positional's meaning differs by command, so the same word reads two ways, and a flag has one
    reading on every command, the reason [Scope is a flag on every command, and push resolves its
    own bookmarks](TODO.md#scope-is-a-flag-on-every-command-and-push-resolves-its-own-bookmarks)
    gave for `-s`, and `land`'s for naming `--source` and `--onto`.
  - jj splits the two the same way: a bookmark name is a revision symbol, and a command that moves
    a bookmark takes its name apart from the revision, `jj bookmark set NAME -r REV` and `jj git
    push --named NAME=REV`.
  - The command line is what the user approves, and a flag says what each word is.
  - `run` keeps its trailing arguments, which are the built binary's.
- `-r, --revision` and `--bookmark`: the names the read commands, `lookup`, and `commit` already
  use, and jj's.
- An old positional is refused, not dropped, wink's call (2026-10-27): a hidden argument whose error

##### feat: push takes --revision and --bookmark

`push`'s positional goes hidden and refused, `-r` names the commit and `--bookmark` the remote's
name, a new name created tracked, and the refusal helper the other commands reuse.

- `options_flags::retired_positional::refusal`, the one wording every retired positional gets: the
  command, "the positional is retired, every argument is a flag", and the flag form with the value
  in place, so the next two rungs and the other cycle share it.
- `push`'s refusal names `--bookmark` when the value is a local bookmark in the repo `-R` names,
  else `-r`, the lookup made in `to_params` and a failed one only losing the hint.
- Two paths, split on whether REV is the work `@-` by commit id, so `-r @-`, `-r <its chid>`, and
  `-r <its bookmark>` all take the pair's:
  - The pair's path is unchanged but for `--bookmark` taking a new name, set at `@-` by the work
    half's own `bookmark_set` and tracked by its push, the call the opening's bookmark uses.
  - `publish_elsewhere`, which replaces `publish_name`, publishes a name alone: the one bookmark at
    REV, or `--bookmark`'s, at REV or new. A bookmark elsewhere is refused naming `move-bookmark`,
    since push moves a bookmark only along the pair's line.
- `-s p` resolves its bookmark the pair's way, so a named bookmark off the line is refused there too,
  where it was moved sideways before.
- `-r` with `-s a` is refused, and `--bookmark` given a revision names `-r`.
- The backlog's **vc-x1 push: rework the two bookmark parameters** retires, the two spellings gone.
- `tests/cli_sync.rs` called `push -s w main`, and the full validation found it, the one CLI caller
  of the old form.

##### feat: commit and squash-push take flags only

`commit`'s `[REV]` becomes `-r`, and `squash-push`'s `[BOOKMARK]` becomes `--bookmark`, each old
positional refused by the helper.

- `commit -r, --revision`: the field stays `rev`, so nothing past the parse changes, and its errors
  say `-r` where they said `REV`. The refusal always names `-r`, the positional having been a
  revision only.
- `squash-push --bookmark`: the one flag, the positional having had no flag form, and the refusal
  always names `--bookmark`.
- Each refusal is made where the command builds its params, `CommitParams::try_from` and
  `SquashPushArgs::to_params`, before any repo is touched.
- No CLI test and no code called either with its positional. The README's examples and tables did,
  and `support/fixtures/build-dr-1.py`'s `vc-x1 push {bookmark} --title` is left: it is a
  transcript line the builder synthesizes as history, never run.

--title` forms brought to what `commit` does now.

## In Progress

### feat: push, commit, and squash-push take flags only

Picked from `## Todo` as **push takes a revision, and the remote's name for it** (wink + agent,
2026-10-24), widened at its planning to every argument a flag (wink + agent, 2026-10-27), and split
in two: this cycle the three commands that publish, the rest **feat: the other commands take flags
only**.

#### Problem

`push`'s positional is a bookmark, so `push -s b @-` is refused, though git needs only a name on
the remote: `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<name>` publishes any commit under a new name, and `jj
git push --named <name>=<REV>` does the same and creates the local bookmark that tracks it. Filed
from the live testing of **feat: vc-x1 closing and land**, whose `[9]` made the refusal say to
leave the revision out.

A positional means something different from command to command: a bookmark to `push` and
`squash-push`, a revision to `commit` and the read commands. So `push -s b feature` has two
readings, the bookmark to move or the commit it is at, and `push` takes its bookmark both as the
positional and as `--bookmark`, one value under two spellings.

#### Solution

- Every argument is a flag, the command names aside, and this cycle does `push`, `commit`, and
  `squash-push`.
- `push -s b|w|a|p [-r REV] [--bookmark NAME]`:
  - REV is the commit to publish, `@-` by default. At `@-` it is the pair's path, unchanged.
    Elsewhere a name alone is published, no pair, today's off-line case, the working copy and the
    root refused.
  - NAME is the remote's name for it, the bookmark at or nearest below REV by default. With no
    bookmark there NAME is required, created at REV and pushed tracked, as `--named` does.
  - A REV that resolves to more than one commit is refused with the count.
- `commit -r REV`, `@` by default, its `--bookmark` unchanged.
- `squash-push --bookmark NAME`.
- An old positional is kept hidden and refused with the flag that replaces it: `push -s b @-`
  names `-r @-`, and `push -s b feature` with `feature` a bookmark names `--bookmark feature`.
- The README's sections for the three, and the agent-files' invocations of them.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a test per rule: `push -r` publishes the commit named, `push --bookmark`
with a new name creates it tracked on origin, a REV of several commits is refused, and each
command's old positional is refused naming its flag. Live, from the rung after push's on: `vc-x1-dev
push -s b @-` fails naming `-r @-`, and a rung committed with `--no-push` is published by
`vc-x1-dev push -s b -r @-`.

#### Deliberation

- Flags only, the command names aside, wink's call (2026-10-27).
  - A positional's meaning differs by command, so the same word reads two ways, and a flag has one
    reading on every command, the reason [Scope is a flag on every command, and push resolves its
    own bookmarks](TODO.md#scope-is-a-flag-on-every-command-and-push-resolves-its-own-bookmarks)
    gave for `-s`, and `land`'s for naming `--source` and `--onto`.
  - jj splits the two the same way: a bookmark name is a revision symbol, and a command that moves
    a bookmark takes its name apart from the revision, `jj bookmark set NAME -r REV` and `jj git
    push --named NAME=REV`.
  - The command line is what the user approves, and a flag says what each word is.
  - `run` keeps its trailing arguments, which are the built binary's.
- `-r, --revision` and `--bookmark`: the names the read commands, `lookup`, and `commit` already
  use, and jj's.
- An old positional is refused, not dropped, wink's call (2026-10-27): a hidden argument whose error
  names the flag, so a stale doc or a habit is told its own fix.
- Two cycles, wink's call (2026-10-27): this one the three commands that publish, which every rung
  runs and the push Todo is about, and the rest in **feat: the other commands take flags only**,
  with **build, install, and run take --dev** folded into it, which keeps `install-dev`, run at
  every rung here, unchanged until this cycle lands, and **init and clone take --scope por**,
  whose commands it touches.
- A REV other than `@-` publishes a name alone, provisional: the pair's checks, the trailer, the
  partner, and the restamp, assume `@-`, and a pair's commit below `@-` was published by its own
  rung.
- The README states the rule in the other cycle, once it holds for every command.
- Waiver, wink's "Continue and complete this cycle except for landing on main" (2026-10-27), after
  the opening's push.
  - Covers every rung from **feat: push takes --revision and --bookmark** through the closing: the
    work review, the description review, the per-push approval, and the hard stop after each push.
  - Does not cover Land: the closing is pushed without `--land`, and the close-out shape is the
    default, trapezoid, until wink chooses at the Land.
  - Validation still runs before every push.

##### feat: push, commit, and squash-push take flags only opening

Opens the cycle: the Todo moved here and widened, the other commands' Todo filed, the version
bumped.

##### feat: push takes --revision and --bookmark

`push`'s positional goes hidden and refused, `-r` names the commit and `--bookmark` the remote's
name, a new name created tracked, and the refusal helper the other commands reuse.

- `options_flags::retired_positional::refusal`, the one wording every retired positional gets: the
  command, "the positional is retired, every argument is a flag", and the flag form with the value
  in place, so the next two rungs and the other cycle share it.
- `push`'s refusal names `--bookmark` when the value is a local bookmark in the repo `-R` names,
  else `-r`, the lookup made in `to_params` and a failed one only losing the hint.
- Two paths, split on whether REV is the work `@-` by commit id, so `-r @-`, `-r <its chid>`, and
  `-r <its bookmark>` all take the pair's:
  - The pair's path is unchanged but for `--bookmark` taking a new name, set at `@-` by the work
    half's own `bookmark_set` and tracked by its push, the call the opening's bookmark uses.
  - `publish_elsewhere`, which replaces `publish_name`, publishes a name alone: the one bookmark at
    REV, or `--bookmark`'s, at REV or new. A bookmark elsewhere is refused naming `move-bookmark`,
    since push moves a bookmark only along the pair's line.
- `-s p` resolves its bookmark the pair's way, so a named bookmark off the line is refused there too,
  where it was moved sideways before.
- `-r` with `-s a` is refused, and `--bookmark` given a revision names `-r`.
- The backlog's **vc-x1 push: rework the two bookmark parameters** retires, the two spellings gone.
- `tests/cli_sync.rs` called `push -s w main`, and the full validation found it, the one CLI caller
  of the old form.

##### feat: commit and squash-push take flags only

`commit`'s `[REV]` becomes `-r`, and `squash-push`'s `[BOOKMARK]` becomes `--bookmark`, each old
positional refused by the helper.

- `commit -r, --revision`: the field stays `rev`, so nothing past the parse changes, and its errors
  say `-r` where they said `REV`. The refusal always names `-r`, the positional having been a
  revision only.
- `squash-push --bookmark`: the one flag, the positional having had no flag form, and the refusal
  always names `--bookmark`.
- Each refusal is made where the command builds its params, `CommitParams::try_from` and
  `SquashPushArgs::to_params`, before any repo is touched.
- No CLI test and no code called either with its positional. The README's examples and tables did,
  and `support/fixtures/build-dr-1.py`'s `vc-x1 push {bookmark} --title` is left: it is a
  transcript line the builder synthesizes as history, never run.

##### docs: the agent-files name the flags

The invocations of the three in `AGENTS.md` and `agent-data/`, with the stale `vc-x1 push <bookmark>
--title` forms brought to what `commit` does now.

##### feat: push, commit, and squash-push take flags only closing

Closing out the cycle.

rand = "0.10"
rand_chacha = "0.10"
serde_json = "1"

[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]
libc = "0.2"

### Committing vs pushing

A cycle rung is committed *by* `vc-x1 push`, never pre-committed with `jj commit`
([why](agent-data/rationale.md#committing-vs-pushing)). "Commit", "push",
and "commit + push" all mean `vc-x1 push`. A bare `jj commit` is asked for by name and is for local
saves and [local ladder](#local-ladders) intermediates. What push does is in [vc-x1 push][vpush].

### Commit description

The title is a Conventional Commit, distinct within its cycle ([Commit titles and
descriptions][cdd]).
The body is in [Commit-body form](agent-data/prose.md#commit-body-form): no version, file list, or
deliberation ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#commit-description)).

### Pushing

Pushing is by `vc-x1 push`. The bookmark moves (create, land, trapezoid) use `jj git push` as jj.md
names, until vc-x1 owns them.

#### Before any push

([why](agent-data/rationale.md#before-any-push))

- This specific push has the user's explicit approval, or an explicit waiver covers it.
- Validation ran, and passed, after the last edit.
- Closing words are written. Nothing follows the turn's final push.

#### At rest: push, stop, squash-push

The contract that keeps both repos clean, the rule **Hard stop after the final push** its first
item's tail ([why](agent-data/rationale.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push)):

1. The agent publishes: completing a step means issuing its publishing command. The agent says what
   is worth saying *before* the final publishing command, responds with the one word "Published",
   and does nothing further until the user speaks.
2. The user squash-pushes: `vc-x1 squash-push -R <agent-dir>` whenever they want both repos fully
