## vc-x1 push: what it does and does not do

`vc-x1 push <bookmark> --yes --title "..." --body "..."` commits both repos with the approved title
and body (`--yes` because push's gates need a tty the agent sandbox lacks, and the user's approval
of the shown title and body already covers them), stamps each new commit's `ochid:` trailer
([above](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), pushes the work bookmark, and squash-pushes the agent
repo's `main`. Three behaviors to keep in mind:

- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 runs no build or tests. Validation is the per-rung
  flow's job, run *before* the push. The one check that remains is `push-work` verifying the
  bookmark's remote refs are tracked.
- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume: every stage no-ops when its work is
  already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If push exits after `push-work` but before
  the agent-repo publish, `vc-x1 squash-push -R <agent-dir>` by hand is the rest of it.
- **`ochid:` trailers are stamped by push** ([No hand-written
  trailers](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), never hand-written into `--title` or `--body`.

## In Progress

### feat: push, commit, and squash-push take flags only

Picked from `## Todo` as **push takes a revision, and the remote's name for it** (wink + agent,
2026-10-24), widened at its planning to every argument a flag (wink + agent, 2026-10-27), and split
in two: this cycle the three commands that publish, the rest **feat: the other commands take flags
only**.

#### Problem

`push`'s positional is a bookmark, so `push -s b @-` is refused, though git needs only a name on
the remote: `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<name>` publishes any commit under a new name, and `jj
git push --named <name>=<REV>` does the same and creates the local bookmark that tracks it. Filed
from the live testing of **feat: vc-x1 closing and land**, whose `[9]` made the refusal say to
leave the revision out.

A positional means something different from command to command: a bookmark to `push` and
`squash-push`, a revision to `commit` and the read commands. So `push -s b feature` has two
readings, the bookmark to move or the commit it is at, and `push` takes its bookmark both as the
positional and as `--bookmark`, one value under two spellings.

#### Solution

- Every argument is a flag, the command names aside, and this cycle does `push`, `commit`, and
  `squash-push`.
- `push -s b|w|a|p [-r REV] [--bookmark NAME]`:
  - REV is the commit to publish, `@-` by default. At `@-` it is the pair's path, unchanged.
    Elsewhere a name alone is published, no pair, today's off-line case, the working copy and the
    root refused.
  - NAME is the remote's name for it, the bookmark at or nearest below REV by default. With no
    bookmark there NAME is required, created at REV and pushed tracked, as `--named` does.
  - A REV that resolves to more than one commit is refused with the count.
- `commit -r REV`, `@` by default, its `--bookmark` unchanged.
- `squash-push --bookmark NAME`.
- An old positional is kept hidden and refused with the flag that replaces it: `push -s b @-`
  names `-r @-`, and `push -s b feature` with `feature` a bookmark names `--bookmark feature`.
- The README's sections for the three, and the agent-files' invocations of them.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a test per rule: `push -r` publishes the commit named, `push --bookmark`
with a new name creates it tracked on origin, a REV of several commits is refused, and each
command's old positional is refused naming its flag. Live, from the rung after push's on: `vc-x1-dev
push -s b @-` fails naming `-r @-`, and a rung committed with `--no-push` is published by
`vc-x1-dev push -s b -r @-`.

#### Deliberation

- Flags only, the command names aside, wink's call (2026-10-27).
  - A positional's meaning differs by command, so the same word reads two ways, and a flag has one
    reading on every command, the reason [Scope is a flag on every command, and push resolves its
    own bookmarks](TODO.md#scope-is-a-flag-on-every-command-and-push-resolves-its-own-bookmarks)
    gave for `-s`, and `land`'s for naming `--source` and `--onto`.
  - jj splits the two the same way: a bookmark name is a revision symbol, and a command that moves
    a bookmark takes its name apart from the revision, `jj bookmark set NAME -r REV` and `jj git
    push --named NAME=REV`.
  - The command line is what the user approves, and a flag says what each word is.
  - `run` keeps its trailing arguments, which are the built binary's.
- `-r, --revision` and `--bookmark`: the names the read commands, `lookup`, and `commit` already
  use, and jj's.
- An old positional is refused, not dropped, wink's call (2026-10-27): a hidden argument whose error
  names the flag, so a stale doc or a habit is told its own fix.
- Two cycles, wink's call (2026-10-27): this one the three commands that publish, which every rung
  runs and the push Todo is about, and the rest in **feat: the other commands take flags only**,
  with **build, install, and run take --dev** folded into it, which keeps `install-dev`, run at
  every rung here, unchanged until this cycle lands, and **init and clone take --scope por**,
  whose commands it touches.
- A REV other than `@-` publishes a name alone, provisional: the pair's checks, the trailer, the
  partner, and the restamp, assume `@-`, and a pair's commit below `@-` was published by its own
  rung.
- The README states the rule in the other cycle, once it holds for every command.
- Waiver, wink's "Continue and complete this cycle except for landing on main" (2026-10-27), after
  the opening's push.
  - Covers every rung from **feat: push takes --revision and --bookmark** through the closing: the
    work review, the description review, the per-push approval, and the hard stop after each push.
  - Does not cover Land: the closing is pushed without `--land`, and the close-out shape is the
    default, trapezoid, until wink chooses at the Land.
  - Validation still runs before every push.

Opens the cycle: the Todo moved here and widened, the other commands' Todo filed, the version

##### feat: push takes --revision and --bookmark

`push`'s positional goes hidden and refused, `-r` names the commit and `--bookmark` the remote's
name, a new name created tracked, and the refusal helper the other commands reuse.

- `options_flags::retired_positional::refusal`, the one wording every retired positional gets: the
  command, "the positional is retired, every argument is a flag", and the flag form with the value
  in place, so the next two rungs and the other cycle share it.
- `push`'s refusal names `--bookmark` when the value is a local bookmark in the repo `-R` names,
  else `-r`, the lookup made in `to_params` and a failed one only losing the hint.
- Two paths, split on whether REV is the work `@-` by commit id, so `-r @-`, `-r <its chid>`, and
  `-r <its bookmark>` all take the pair's:
  - The pair's path is unchanged but for `--bookmark` taking a new name, set at `@-` by the work
    half's own `bookmark_set` and tracked by its push, the call the opening's bookmark uses.
  - `publish_elsewhere`, which replaces `publish_name`, publishes a name alone: the one bookmark at
    REV, or `--bookmark`'s, at REV or new. A bookmark elsewhere is refused naming `move-bookmark`,
    since push moves a bookmark only along the pair's line.
- `-s p` resolves its bookmark the pair's way, so a named bookmark off the line is refused there too,
  where it was moved sideways before.
- `-r` with `-s a` is refused, and `--bookmark` given a revision names `-r`.
- The backlog's **vc-x1 push: rework the two bookmark parameters** retires, the two spellings gone.
- `tests/cli_sync.rs` called `push -s w main`, and the full validation found it, the one CLI caller
  of the old form.

##### feat: commit and squash-push take flags only

`commit`'s `[REV]` becomes `-r`, and `squash-push`'s `[BOOKMARK]` becomes `--bookmark`, each old
positional refused by the helper.

- `commit -r, --revision`: the field stays `rev`, so nothing past the parse changes, and its errors
  say `-r` where they said `REV`. The refusal always names `-r`, the positional having been a
  revision only.
- `squash-push --bookmark`: the one flag, the positional having had no flag form, and the refusal
  always names `--bookmark`.
- Each refusal is made where the command builds its params, `CommitParams::try_from` and
  `SquashPushArgs::to_params`, before any repo is touched.
- No CLI test and no code called either with its positional. The README's examples and tables did,
  and `support/fixtures/build-dr-1.py`'s `vc-x1 push {bookmark} --title` is left: it is a
  transcript line the builder synthesizes as history, never run.

--title` forms brought to what `commit` does now.

content.content:
conventional-commit shape.
- [Code conventions](../agent-data/code.md): doc comments, `// OK: ...` on `unwrap*` calls.

Per-cycle workflow is AGENTS.md's [Cycle protocol](../AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol):

- [Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening): the bookmark, the six provisional items, the ladder.
- [The per-rung flow](../AGENTS.md#the-per-rung-flow): validation, the work and description
  review stops, `vc-x1 push`.
- [Commit description](../AGENTS.md#commit-description): Conventional Commits title, body shape
  per work vs agent repo.
- [Pushing](../AGENTS.md#pushing): push policy, the at-rest contract.
- [Close-out](../AGENTS.md#close-out): acceptance check, the chores move, shape, landing.
# Agent-files size

The line count of the agent-files, one row per landing that changed them, so the set's size is
tracked over time. A cycle that leaves the agent-files untouched adds no row, since a row saying
the count did not move records nothing. Smaller is the quasi-goal: a rule stated once is shorter
than a rule stated three times, and a shrinking count is evidence the set is converging, while a
growing one is a prompt to ask what arrived as a paragraph that should have been a line. The count
is not a rule, and a rule is never cut to move it.

A finding from the proposal cycle (2026-08-27), for whoever next tries a cut: a draft that cut
AGENTS.md from 370 to 320 lines with every rule kept found that the remaining bulk is the rules
themselves, so a further cut has to cut rules, and that is a convention decision, not an edit.

The count is `wc -l` over `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and `agent-data/*.md`, the total leaving out
`rationale.md`, taken at the close-out of a cycle that changed an agent-file and recorded here as
the closing rung's last edit, with the cycle title as the row's label. `rationale.md` is out of the
total because it is the rules' why and grows with every rule that gains one, so a rule gaining a
why does not read as the set growing. Rows before v0.2.5 counted it.

`vc-x1 agent-files size` takes the count and slides the per-file table, a new leftmost column in
and the oldest out. It is dry-run by default and `--no-dry-run` writes the file, `--label=TEXT`
names a column the set's version file cannot, and the `## Counts` row above stays a hand's work,
since its note is prose.

## Counts

| Landed | Cycle | Files | Lines | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-25 | docs: the family agent-files proposal opening | 10 | 2205 | vc-x1's set |
| 2026-08-27 | docs: sync the agent-files to zc-ring-x1's set | 12 | 2822 | two files back, 863 |

# Notes

This directory contains various notes and documentation related to the project. Each file is
organized by topic for easy reference.

The chores-NN.md files in [chores/](chores) and [done.md](done.md) are frozen history: the records
of cycles that closed before the cycle-record rule ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).
Nothing is appended to them. They stay until the agent-repo transcripts are comfortable to read a
cycle from, then both retire in one cycle after a permalink sweep of the links into them (the `##
Waiting` entry in [../TODO.md](../TODO.md)). A cycle's live record is [../TODO.md](../TODO.md)'s `##
In Progress` block, and a closed cycle's is its `## Closed` block in the landmark commit's tree.

On trial since the cycle "feat: sync is safe by default" (2026-10-09), a cycle's record is kept in
[../zDOING.md](../zDOING.md) instead, the agent-files not yet saying so, and that cycle's landmark
holds its finished block there.

Tool architecture lives at the repo root in [`../ARCHITECTURE.md`](../ARCHITECTURE.md): the
CLI-args / `Context`+`Params` split, a generic module map, the subcommand model, and what the
Context+Params port and the options_flags extraction *are* (the *live status* is in the chores
files).

Multi-cycle programs too big for a TODO.md entry get their own dated plan file, e.g.
[refactor-20260716.md](refactor-20260716.md) (typed jj facade -> jj-lib in-process): one `##`
section per stage, so chores and todo entries can reference a stage by anchor. The plan file owns
the forward design, and chores still records each shipped cycle.

A rule that governs what the tool does, rather than a record of what was done, gets its own topic
file so it can be found without knowing which cycle produced it, e.g.
[jj-version-policy.md](jj-version-policy.md). The investigation behind such a rule stays where it
happened (a plan file or a chores section) and is linked from the policy, so neither restates the
other.

The agent-files' line count over time is in [agent-files-size.md](agent-files-size.md), one row
per landing, smaller being the quasi-goal. `vc-x1 agent-files size` takes the count and slides
that file's per-file window.

The session lock, `.agent-running`, and what two agent sessions in one workspace do without it,
are in [session-lock.md](session-lock.md): what Claude Code's hooks could do in the agent's place,
three tests of two sessions with no lock, and what was decided. The lock is off, and the file
keeps the instruction that took it and what turning it on again would want settled. How to turn
it on and check it is in the [README](../README.md#the-session-lock).

How a change to a line in any work-repo file is connected to its discussion in the agent-repo,
the partner commit, its time-window, and the transcript write, is in
[transcript-write.md](transcript-write.md). It carries the objective and the terms, the by-hand
procedure, the two decisions the probes settled, the `vc-x1 lookup` command's requirements in
their one home, what building the command found, and the probes themselves, three cycles of them.
`vc-x1 lookup` does the procedure in both directions, and the fixture it is tested over is built
by `support/fixtures/build-dr-1.py` into the workspace's gitignored `.fixtures/`, which
`[test] fixtures` names, so a fresh clone builds its own. What the fixture holds, and the case
each of its cycles exists for, is in [fixture-dr-1.md](fixture-dr-1.md).

In the future I expect we may want to create a "notes" database to better manage the information,
TBD.

Examples chore file:
```
# Chores-01.md
 
General maintenance tasks and considerations for the project see other files for
more specific topics. A chore in a chores file provides quick information on the
how and why of a particular chore.

## Create a binary that lists jj info 

This binary should list the changeID, commitID, and description title
and using `jj-lib`
```

## Workflow and conventions

Bot-facing workflow and conventions live in [`../AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md) (hard rules + file
map) and its `../agent-data/` satellites:

- [Notes file conventions](../agent-data/notes.md): Todo format, Reference numbering, Notes
  references (`[[N]]` citation style), Markdown anchor links, Retiring Done entries, Chores
  conventions (section headers / Done entries exact-title rule, content rules, the as-built
  ladder and its commit reference format, the chores Table of Contents).
- [Prose and durable text](../agent-data/prose.md): prose form, typeable punctuation,
  conventional-commit shape.
- [Code conventions](../agent-data/code.md): doc comments, `// OK: ...` on `unwrap*` calls.

Per-cycle workflow is AGENTS.md's [Cycle protocol](../AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol):

- [Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening): the bookmark, the six provisional items, the ladder.
- [The per-rung flow](../AGENTS.md#the-per-rung-flow): validation, the work and description

- [Commit description](../AGENTS.md#commit-description): Conventional Commits title, body shape
  per work vs agent repo.
- [Pushing](../AGENTS.md#pushing): push policy, the at-rest contract.
- [Close-out](../AGENTS.md#close-out): acceptance check, the chores move, shape, landing.

## In Progress

### feat: push, commit, and squash-push take flags only

Picked from `## Todo` as **push takes a revision, and the remote's name for it** (wink + agent,
2026-10-24), widened at its planning to every argument a flag (wink + agent, 2026-10-27), and split
in two: this cycle the three commands that publish, the rest **feat: the other commands take flags
only**.

#### Problem

`push`'s positional is a bookmark, so `push -s b @-` is refused, though git needs only a name on
the remote: `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<name>` publishes any commit under a new name, and `jj
git push --named <name>=<REV>` does the same and creates the local bookmark that tracks it. Filed
from the live testing of **feat: vc-x1 closing and land**, whose `[9]` made the refusal say to
leave the revision out.

A positional means something different from command to command: a bookmark to `push` and
`squash-push`, a revision to `commit` and the read commands. So `push -s b feature` has two
readings, the bookmark to move or the commit it is at, and `push` takes its bookmark both as the
positional and as `--bookmark`, one value under two spellings.

#### Solution

- Every argument is a flag, the command names aside, and this cycle does `push`, `commit`, and
  `squash-push`.
- `push -s b|w|a|p [-r REV] [--bookmark NAME]`:
  - REV is the commit to publish, `@-` by default. At `@-` it is the pair's path, unchanged.
    Elsewhere a name alone is published, no pair, today's off-line case, the working copy and the
    root refused.
  - NAME is the remote's name for it, the bookmark at or nearest below REV by default. With no
    bookmark there NAME is required, created at REV and pushed tracked, as `--named` does.
  - A REV that resolves to more than one commit is refused with the count.
- `commit -r REV`, `@` by default, its `--bookmark` unchanged.
- `squash-push --bookmark NAME`.
- An old positional is kept hidden and refused with the flag that replaces it: `push -s b @-`
  names `-r @-`, and `push -s b feature` with `feature` a bookmark names `--bookmark feature`.
- The README's sections for the three, and the agent-files' invocations of them.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a test per rule: `push -r` publishes the commit named, `push --bookmark`
with a new name creates it tracked on origin, a REV of several commits is refused, and each
command's old positional is refused naming its flag. Live, from the rung after push's on: `vc-x1-dev
push -s b @-` fails naming `-r @-`, and a rung committed with `--no-push` is published by
`vc-x1-dev push -s b -r @-`.

#### Deliberation

- Flags only, the command names aside, wink's call (2026-10-27).
  - A positional's meaning differs by command, so the same word reads two ways, and a flag has one
    reading on every command, the reason [Scope is a flag on every command, and push resolves its
    own bookmarks](TODO.md#scope-is-a-flag-on-every-command-and-push-resolves-its-own-bookmarks)
    gave for `-s`, and `land`'s for naming `--source` and `--onto`.
  - jj splits the two the same way: a bookmark name is a revision symbol, and a command that moves
    a bookmark takes its name apart from the revision, `jj bookmark set NAME -r REV` and `jj git
    push --named NAME=REV`.
  - The command line is what the user approves, and a flag says what each word is.
  - `run` keeps its trailing arguments, which are the built binary's.
- `-r, --revision` and `--bookmark`: the names the read commands, `lookup`, and `commit` already
  use, and jj's.
- An old positional is refused, not dropped, wink's call (2026-10-27): a hidden argument whose error
  names the flag, so a stale doc or a habit is told its own fix.
- Two cycles, wink's call (2026-10-27): this one the three commands that publish, which every rung
  runs and the push Todo is about, and the rest in **feat: the other commands take flags only**,
  with **build, install, and run take --dev** folded into it, which keeps `install-dev`, run at
  every rung here, unchanged until this cycle lands, and **init and clone take --scope por**,
  whose commands it touches.
- A REV other than `@-` publishes a name alone, provisional: the pair's checks, the trailer, the
  partner, and the restamp, assume `@-`, and a pair's commit below `@-` was published by its own
  rung.
- The README states the rule in the other cycle, once it holds for every command.
- Waiver, wink's "Continue and complete this cycle except for landing on main" (2026-10-27), after
  the opening's push.
  - Covers every rung from **feat: push takes --revision and --bookmark** through the closing: the
    work review, the description review, the per-push approval, and the hard stop after each push.
  - Does not cover Land: the closing is pushed without `--land`, and the close-out shape is the
    default, trapezoid, until wink chooses at the Land.
  - Validation still runs before every push.

#### Solution

What was done:

- Every argument is a flag, the command names aside, and this cycle did `push`, `commit`, and
  `squash-push`, each old positional kept hidden and refused by one helper,
  `options_flags::retired_positional::refusal`, naming the flag with the value in place.
- `push -s b|w|a|p [-r REV] [--bookmark NAME]`:
  - REV is the commit to publish, `@-` by default, one commit, a REV of several refused with the
    count. REV is the work `@-` by commit id, however it is spelled, for the pair's path.

- **What landed on the bookmark** (all pushed, nothing on `main` yet):

content.text:
The positionals are gone as a way to pass anything. All three commands now take only flags, and that's what the title means. What's left is a hidden argument whose only job is to fail with a useful message.

- **What you see:** `--help` and the README no longer list a positional for `push`, `commit`, or `squash-push`. They show `-r` and `--bookmark` only.
- **What happens if you type one anyway:** it's an error, and nothing runs. From the live check:
  ```
  $ vc-x1-dev push -s b @-
  error: push: the positional is retired, every argument is a flag: `-r @-`
  ```
- **Why the hidden argument exists:** that was your "hidden positional error" choice. Without it, clap would reject the word with its generic "unexpected argument '@-' found" and wouldn't say which flag to use. The hidden argument only catches the word so the error can name `-r @-` or `--bookmark feature`. A value there is never used.

So the positional can't be used, only refused. If you'd rather drop even the hidden argument and accept clap's generic error, that's a small change: remove the `retired` field from the three argument structs and the tests that check the message. The bookmark is still unlanded, so I could add it as a rung. Do you want that, or keep the guided error?

=== config
vc-x1 0.85.13+2461cdfcb0c8

Print settable config keys and their defaults

Usage: vc-x1 config [OPTIONS] [TARGET]

Arguments:
  [TARGET]
          What to print or validate: side keyword(s) `work`, `agent`,
          `work,agent`, or a config-file path. The user config
          (`~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`) has no keyword: pass its
          path.
          
          [default: work,agent]

=== validate-config
vc-x1 0.85.13+2461cdfcb0c8

Check a workspace's config files.

Verifies every key is one the schema declares for that side,
the legacy schema is rejected, a dual workspace's two [repos]
registries agree, the file's own links resolve, and a side's
config carries `repos.work`. Read-only; exits non-zero when
anything is found. Was `config --validate` before 0.80.6.

Usage: vc-x1 validate-config [OPTIONS] [TARGET]

Arguments:
  [TARGET]
          What to check: side keyword(s) `work`, `agent`,
          `work,agent`, or a config-file path. The user config
          (`~/.config/vc-x1/config.toml`) has no keyword: pass its
          path.
          
          [default: work,agent]

=== clone
vc-x1 0.85.13+2461cdfcb0c8

Clone a dual-repo project

Usage: vc-x1 clone [OPTIONS] <TARGET> [NAME]

Arguments:
  <TARGET>
          Source to clone: URL or local path.
          
          - URL: `git@host:owner/name(.git)?`, `https://...(.git)?`
          - A slashed source with no path prefix (`owner/name`) is
            refused: it reads equally as a path and as the retired
            owner/name shorthand, so pass `./owner/name` or a URL.
          - Local path: `./X`, `../X`, `/X`, `~/X`, `~`, `.`, `..`
            (passed directly to `git clone`)

  [NAME]
          Destination dir name in cwd [default: derived from TARGET]

=== init
vc-x1 0.85.13+2461cdfcb0c8

Create a new dual-repo project

Usage: vc-x1 init [OPTIONS] <TARGET> [NAME]

Arguments:
  <TARGET>
          Target: URL, path, or bare NAME.
          
          - URL: `git@host:owner/name(.git)?`, `https://...(.git)?`,
            used as-is, config not consulted.
          - Path: `./X`, `../X`, `/X`, `~/X`, `~`, `.`, `..`, is the
            directory path, remote resolved via `--repo` chain.
          - Bare NAME: becomes NAME.git, remote resolved via
            `--repo` chain.
          
          A slashed target with no path prefix (`owner/name`) is
          refused: it reads equally as a path and as the retired
          owner/name shorthand, so pass `./owner/name` or a URL.

  [NAME]
          Repo directory name override (URL form only).
          
          - URL form: repo created at `cwd/<NAME>` instead of the
            URL-derived name.
          - Path / bare-NAME forms: error if given (TARGET already
            names the repo).

=== symlink
vc-x1 0.85.13+2461cdfcb0c8

Create Claude Code project symlink

Usage: vc-x1 symlink [OPTIONS] [TARGET]

Arguments:
  [TARGET]
          Directory to link to [default: from repos.agent, else .claude]

=== agent-session
vc-x1 0.85.13+2461cdfcb0c8

Display a Claude Code agent session transcript (.jsonl) as a
readable conversation.

Output is a set of items (headers, user, assistant, tool,
thinking, results, meta, summary) each toggled by --<item> /
--no-<item> (last one wins), with --all / --none as bulk bases.
The default set (headers, user, assistant, tool, summary) can
be replaced by [agent-session].items in the user config
(comma-separated list); CLI flags then adjust the resolved
set. Malformed lines (e.g. a live session's truncated last
line) warn to stderr and never fail the run.

Alternate views: --fields (field inventory per entry type),
--unknown (only unmodeled paths: how the format moved), and
--raw (pretty-printed source lines). --lines slices by source
JSONL line: the same unit in every view.

Usage: vc-x1 agent-session [OPTIONS] <FILE>

Arguments:
  <FILE>
          Session transcript .jsonl file to display

=== lookup
vc-x1 0.85.13+2461cdfcb0c8

Resolve a line in either repo of a dual workspace to the
window of lines in the other repo.

`lookup [SCOPE] FILE:LINE`: SCOPE is the side the line is on,
`work` or `agent`, and FILE:LINE is the form editors, compilers,
and grep print. SCOPE is inferred from the file's path when
omitted, and with SCOPE given a path relative to that side's
repo root works from anywhere. A named SCOPE the path disagrees
with is an error. The line must exist in the file on disk.

Usage: vc-x1 lookup [OPTIONS] <SCOPE|FILE:LINE> [FILE:LINE]

Arguments:
  <SCOPE|FILE:LINE>
          `SCOPE FILE:LINE`, or `FILE:LINE` alone: SCOPE is the side the line is
          on, `work` or `agent`, inferred from the path when omitted

  [FILE:LINE]
          `FILE:LINE` when the first argument is SCOPE

## In Progress

### feat: the other commands take flags only

Picked from `## Todo` as **feat: the other commands take flags only** (wink + agent, 2026-10-27),
split from **feat: push, commit, and squash-push take flags only**, with **build, install, and run
take --dev** and **init and clone take --scope por** folded in at that cycle's opening, and the
`agent-files` subcommands added at this one's.

#### Problem

**feat: push, commit, and squash-push take flags only** made every argument of the three commands
that publish a flag, and the rest still take positionals: a revision and a count on the read
commands, a scope or a file on `lookup`, a file on the file commands, a side or a path on `config`
and `validate-config`, directories on the `agent-files` subcommands, and a source or target and a
name on `init`, `clone`, and `symlink`. So a word on the command line still reads by its place, and
the rule is not yet one the README can state.

Two of the folded entries are the same kind of problem:

- `build-dev`, `install-dev`, and `run-dev` are `build`, `install`, and `run` with the dev build,
  each's help saying so, and a suffix reads as a command of its own, so `land-dev` seemed a
  two-step Land. Found at **feat: vc-x1 land** (wink + agent, 2026-10-26).
- `init` and `clone` alone spell the single-repo form `--por`, where the write commands spell it
  `-s p|por`, and creating a POR from the docs took four tries: `init --por <name>` stops on "no
  account specified", `--account` is read as a GitHub owner when it names an `[account.<name>]`
  section, and only the URL target, which needs no config, works (wink + agent, 2026-10-26).

#### Solution

Every argument a flag, the command names aside, each old positional kept hidden and refused with
the flag that replaces it by `options_flags::retired_positional::refusal`, as the first cycle did.
The flag names marked provisional are settled at their rung.

- `chid`, `desc`, `list`, `show`, `validate-desc`, `fix-desc`: `[REVISION] [COMMITS]` go, since
  `-r, --revision` and `-n, --commits` are there already.
- `lookup`: the side is `-s`, which [Scope is a flag on every command, and push resolves its own
  bookmarks](TODO.md#scope-is-a-flag-on-every-command-and-push-resolves-its-own-bookmarks) already
  asks for, and the line `--line FILE:LINE`.
- `agent-session --file PATH`, `validate-anchors --file PATH`, repeatable, and `validate-todo` and
  `fix-todo --file PATH`, `TODO.md` by default.
- `config` and `validate-config`: `[TARGET]`, a side keyword or a path, splits into `-s` for the
  side, `work,agent` by default, and `--file PATH` for a config file, the user config included.
- `agent-files diff --from A --to B`, `agent-files copy --from SRC --to DST`, and `agent-files size
  --dir DIR`, provisional, their defaults unchanged.
- `init --target URL|PATH|NAME --name NAME`, provisional, `--repo` being taken, `clone --from
  URL|PATH --name NAME`, provisional, and `symlink --target PATH`.
- `init` and `clone` take `-s/--scope`, `both` by default and `por`, `work` and `agent` refused,
  and `--por` errors naming `--scope por`:
  - the dual-only and POR-only checks (`--config`, `--agent-dir`, `--agent-repo`, `--agent-suffix`,
    `--use-template`'s `,BOT`) move to the scope
  - the no-account and unknown-account errors name the URL target as the way that needs no config,
    the user config's path, and a minimal `[account.<name>]` section
  - stale help fixed: init's "Create a new dual-repo project" and `--por`'s "`.claude/`
    companion", `--use-template`'s `--scope=por`, and `--config`'s `.vc-config.toml`.
- `build`, `install`, and `run` take `-d/--dev`, choosing the config's `release`/`dev` pairs, and
  `--release` the release profile, so `install --dev --release` installs a release candidate beside
  the landed binary. `build-dev`, `install-dev`, and `run-dev` stay as hidden commands refused with
  the new spelling. `run` keeps its trailing arguments, the built binary's, `--dev` before them.
- The README states the rule in its CLI section, and every command's section and summary line uses
  the flags. `clippy.toml`'s spawn register entry 7, the completion tests, and the agent-files'
  `install-dev`, the last told to **agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1**.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a test per command that its old positional is refused naming its flag,
and per renamed `-dev` command that it is refused naming `--dev`. Every subcommand's `vc-x1-dev
<cmd> --help` Usage line shows no positional, `run`'s trailing `[ARGS]...` aside. Live: `vc-x1-dev
install --dev` installs the dev build as `vc-x1-dev`, `vc-x1-dev run --dev -- -V` prints the dev
build's banner, `vc-x1-dev show -s both @-` is refused naming `-r @-`, and `vc-x1-dev init -s por
--target <url> --dry-run` plans a POR.

#### Deliberation

- One cycle for the rest, the folded entries with it, wink's call (2026-10-27): each is a command's
  arguments brought to the flags, and the README states the rule once all of them hold it.
- The `agent-files` subcommands join at this opening: the Todo entry listed the commands from the
  top-level help, and `diff`, `copy`, and `size` take directories by position.
- `config` and `validate-config` split `[TARGET]` in two, since it takes a side keyword or a path
  in one place, the ambiguity the rule removes, and `-s` is what a side is everywhere else.
- `init --target`, not `--repo`, which already names the remote's category and value.
- The `-dev` rung comes last among the commands, since every rung before it installs with
  `install-dev`, and from it on the cycle installs with `install --dev`.

#### Ladder

- [feat: the other commands take flags only opening][o0] (current)
- [feat: the read commands take -r and -n only][o1]
- [feat: lookup takes -s and --line][o2]
- [feat: the file commands take --file][o3]
- [feat: config and validate-config take -s and --file][o4]
- [feat: agent-files diff, copy, and size take flags][o5]
- [feat: init, clone, and symlink take flags and --scope por][o6]
- [feat: build, install, and run take --dev][o7]
- [docs: the README states every argument is a flag][o8]
- [feat: the other commands take flags only closing][o9]

# Doing: the cycle record

What is being done: the running cycle's planning and its work's documentation. The last
finished cycle's is in [zCLOSED.md](zCLOSED.md), and what we might do is in [TODO.md](TODO.md). The
block's shape is on trial: it opens with the Todo as it was picked from `TODO.md`, then the
Deliberation, the plan, Solution and Acceptance check, and the Ladder with its details.

This file is a trial (2026-10-09). The agent-files still name `TODO.md > ## In Progress` as the
record's home, and the cycle that makes this file the rule is [The cycle-record moves out of
TODO.md into zDOING.md](TODO.md#the-cycle-record-moves-out-of-todomd-into-zdoingmd).

## Continuation notes

Where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a record: read first, acted
on, and reset to `_None._` by the reader. Kept here by the trial and no longer in `TODO.md`,
where [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint) still says to look.

_None._

## In Progress

### feat: the other commands take flags only

Picked from `## Todo` as **feat: the other commands take flags only** (wink + agent, 2026-10-27),
split from **feat: push, commit, and squash-push take flags only**, with **build, install, and run
take --dev** and **init and clone take --scope por** folded in at that cycle's opening, and the
`agent-files` subcommands added at this one's.

#### Problem

**feat: push, commit, and squash-push take flags only** made every argument of the three commands
that publish a flag, and the rest still take positionals: a revision and a count on the read
commands, a scope or a file on `lookup`, a file on the file commands, a side or a path on `config`
and `validate-config`, directories on the `agent-files` subcommands, and a source or target and a
name on `init`, `clone`, and `symlink`. So a word on the command line still reads by its place, and
the rule is not yet one the README can state.

Two of the folded entries are the same kind of problem:

- `build-dev`, `install-dev`, and `run-dev` are `build`, `install`, and `run` with the dev build,
  each's help saying so, and a suffix reads as a command of its own, so `land-dev` seemed a
  two-step Land. Found at **feat: vc-x1 land** (wink + agent, 2026-10-26).
- `init` and `clone` alone spell the single-repo form `--por`, where the write commands spell it
  `-s p|por`, and creating a POR from the docs took four tries: `init --por <name>` stops on "no
  account specified", `--account` is read as a GitHub owner when it names an `[account.<name>]`
  section, and only the URL target, which needs no config, works (wink + agent, 2026-10-26).

#### Solution

Every argument a flag, the command names aside, each old positional kept hidden and refused with
the flag that replaces it by `options_flags::retired_positional::refusal`, as the first cycle did.
The flag names marked provisional are settled at their rung.

- `chid`, `desc`, `list`, `show`, `validate-desc`, `fix-desc`: `[REVISION] [COMMITS]` go, since
  `-r, --revision` and `-n, --commits` are there already.
- `lookup`: the side is `-s`, which [Scope is a flag on every command, and push resolves its own
  bookmarks](TODO.md#scope-is-a-flag-on-every-command-and-push-resolves-its-own-bookmarks) already
  asks for, and the line `--line FILE:LINE`.
- `agent-session --file PATH`, `validate-anchors --file PATH`, repeatable, and `validate-todo` and
  `fix-todo --file PATH`, `TODO.md` by default.
- `config` and `validate-config`: `[TARGET]`, a side keyword or a path, splits into `-s` for the
  side, `work,agent` by default, and `--file PATH` for a config file, the user config included.
- `agent-files diff --from A --to B`, `agent-files copy --from SRC --to DST`, and `agent-files size
  --dir DIR`, provisional, their defaults unchanged.
- `init --target URL|PATH|NAME --name NAME`, provisional, `--repo` being taken, `clone --from
  URL|PATH --name NAME`, provisional, and `symlink --target PATH`.
- `init` and `clone` take `-s/--scope`, `both` by default and `por`, `work` and `agent` refused,
  and `--por` errors naming `--scope por`:
  - the dual-only and POR-only checks (`--config`, `--agent-dir`, `--agent-repo`, `--agent-suffix`,
    `--use-template`'s `,BOT`) move to the scope
  - the no-account and unknown-account errors name the URL target as the way that needs no config,
    the user config's path, and a minimal `[account.<name>]` section
  - stale help fixed: init's "Create a new dual-repo project" and `--por`'s "`.claude/`
    companion", `--use-template`'s `--scope=por`, and `--config`'s `.vc-config.toml`.
- `build`, `install`, and `run` take `-d/--dev`, choosing the config's `release`/`dev` pairs, and
  `--release` the release profile, so `install --dev --release` installs a release candidate beside
  the landed binary. `build-dev`, `install-dev`, and `run-dev` stay as hidden commands refused with
  the new spelling. `run` keeps its trailing arguments, the built binary's, `--dev` before them.
- The README states the rule in its CLI section, and every command's section and summary line uses
  the flags. `clippy.toml`'s spawn register entry 7, the completion tests, and the agent-files'
  `install-dev`, the last told to **agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1**.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a test per command that its old positional is refused naming its flag,
and per renamed `-dev` command that it is refused naming `--dev`. Every subcommand's `vc-x1-dev
<cmd> --help` Usage line shows no positional, `run`'s trailing `[ARGS]...` aside. Live: `vc-x1-dev
install --dev` installs the dev build as `vc-x1-dev`, `vc-x1-dev run --dev -- -V` prints the dev
build's banner, `vc-x1-dev show -s both @-` is refused naming `-r @-`, and `vc-x1-dev init -s por
--target <url> --dry-run` plans a POR.

#### Deliberation

- One cycle for the rest, the folded entries with it, wink's call (2026-10-27): each is a command's
  arguments brought to the flags, and the README states the rule once all of them hold it.
- The `agent-files` subcommands join at this opening: the Todo entry listed the commands from the
  top-level help, and `diff`, `copy`, and `size` take directories by position.
- `config` and `validate-config` split `[TARGET]` in two, since it takes a side keyword or a path
  in one place, the ambiguity the rule removes, and `-s` is what a side is everywhere else.
- `init --target`, not `--repo`, which already names the remote's category and value.
- The `-dev` rung comes last among the commands, since every rung before it installs with
  `install-dev`, and from it on the cycle installs with `install --dev`.

77	/// Inputs to the validate-desc op, flat, owned, clap-free.
78	///
79	/// Mirrors `ValidateDescArgs`: positional `REVISION` / `COMMITS`
80	/// (`pos_rev` / `pos_count`), `--revision` / `--commits`
81	/// (`revision` / `limit`), `--other-repo`, `--id-len`, and `-s`
82	/// with `-R` resolved into `repos`, each side's label and path in
83	/// scope order.
84	#[derive(Debug)]
85	pub struct ValidateDescParams {
86	    pub pos_rev: Option<String>,
87	    pub pos_count: Option<usize>,
88	    pub revision: String,
89	    pub limit: Option<usize>,
90	    pub repos: Vec<(String, PathBuf)>,
91	    pub other_repo: Option<PathBuf>,
92	    pub id_len: usize,
93	}
94	
95	impl TryFrom<&ValidateDescArgs> for ValidateDescParams {
96	    type Error = String;
97	
98	    /// Resolve `-s` and `-R` into the sides to check, labeled by
99	    /// their keywords, and copy the rest over. `-s p` is refused
100	    /// here, before anything is read.
101	    fn try_from(a: &ValidateDescArgs) -> Result<Self, String> {
102	        let sides = match &a.scope {
103	            RepoScope::Sides(s) => s,
104	            RepoScope::Por => {
105	                return Err(
106	                    "-s p: a plain repo has no other repo to check its descriptions \
107	                            against. validate-desc takes `-s w|a|b` in a dual workspace"
108	                        .to_string(),
109	                );
110	            }
111	        };
112	        let paths = crate::common::resolve_scoped_repos(&a.scope, a.repo.as_deref())
113	            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
114	        let repos = sides
115	            .0
116	            .iter()
117	            .zip(paths)
118	            .map(|(side, path)| (side_keyword(*side).to_string(), path))
119	            .collect();
120	        Ok(Self {
121	            pos_rev: a.pos_rev.clone(),
122	            pos_count: a.pos_count,
123	            revision: a.revision.clone(),
124	            limit: a.limit,
125	            repos,
126	            other_repo: a.other_repo.clone(),
127	            id_len: a.id_len,
128	        })
129	    }
130	}

140	    MissingAmbiguous(usize),  // no ochid, multiple title matches
141	    MissingWithMatch(String), // no ochid, unique title match found
142	}

239	Completions are generated dynamically by the binary, so they stay in sync with the installed version
240	automatically.
241	
242	### Positional shorthand
243	
244	REVISION and COMMITS can be given as positional arguments, omitting `-r` and `-n`:
245	
246	```
247	vc-x1 list x                # just x (1 commit)
248	vc-x1 list x 5              # x.. 5 -> x + 4 ancestors (5 commits)
249	vc-x1 list x.. 5            # same as above
250	vc-x1 list ..x 3            # 2 descendants + x (3 commits)
251	vc-x1 list ..x.. 3          # 1 descendant, x, 1 ancestor (3 commits)
252	vc-x1 list ..x.. 1          # just x (1 commit)
253	```
254	
255	**Defaults:** with no arguments, REVISION is `@` and COMMITS is 1 (just the working copy).
256	
257	Named flags `-r`/`--revision`, `-n`/`--commits`, `-R`/`--repo`, and `-s`/`--scope` take precedence
258	over positional arguments.
259	
260	### Multi-repo queries
261	
262	`-s`/`--scope` selects workspace sides by role keyword. `work` is the work repo, `agent` is the
263	`.claude` repo, `both` (or the spelled-out `work,agent`) is both. The workspace root is found by
264	walking up from cwd (the existing `find_workspace_root` rule).
265	
266	```
267	vc-x1 chid -s work,bot          # both sides of the workspace
268	vc-x1 chid -s work              # just the work repo
269	vc-x1 chid -s agent             # just the bot repo
270	vc-x1 list @.. 3 -s work,bot    # works with chid / desc / list / show
271	```
272	
273	`-R`/`--repo` takes a single path. Used alone it points at one jj repo (workspace lookup is
274	skipped), and combined with `-s` it overrides the workspace root for the role lookup:
275	
276	```
277	vc-x1 chid -R .                  # single repo at .
278	vc-x1 chid -R .claude            # single repo at .claude
279	vc-x1 chid -R ../other -s work,bot   # both sides of ../other workspace
280	```
281	
282	Defaults preserve prior behavior: no flag -> `[.]`, `-R foo` alone -> `[foo]`. When multiple repos
283	are resolved (any `-s` that names more than one role), output is labeled with bold `=== path ===`
284	headers by default. Control the label with `-l`/`--label` and `-L`/`--no-label`:
285

287	vc-x1 chid -s work,agent          # default label: === path ===

289	vc-x1 chid -s work,bot -L         # no label (raw output)

source (COMPLETE=fish vc-x1 | psub)
```

Completions are generated dynamically by the binary, so they stay in sync with the installed version
automatically.

### Positional shorthand

REVISION and COMMITS can be given as positional arguments, omitting `-r` and `-n`:

```
vc-x1 list x                # just x (1 commit)
vc-x1 list x 5              # x.. 5 -> x + 4 ancestors (5 commits)
vc-x1 list x.. 5            # same as above
vc-x1 list ..x 3            # 2 descendants + x (3 commits)
vc-x1 list ..x.. 3          # 1 descendant, x, 1 ancestor (3 commits)
vc-x1 list ..x.. 1          # just x (1 commit)
```

**Defaults:** with no arguments, REVISION is `@` and COMMITS is 1 (just the working copy).

Named flags `-r`/`--revision`, `-n`/`--commits`, `-R`/`--repo`, and `-s`/`--scope` take precedence
over positional arguments.

### Multi-repo queries

`-s`/`--scope` selects workspace sides by role keyword. `work` is the work repo, `agent` is the
`.claude` repo, `both` (or the spelled-out `work,agent`) is both. The workspace root is found by
walking up from cwd (the existing `find_workspace_root` rule).

```
vc-x1 chid -s work,bot          # both sides of the workspace
vc-x1 chid -s work              # just the work repo
vc-x1 chid -s agent             # just the bot repo
vc-x1 list @.. 3 -s work,bot    # works with chid / desc / list / show
```

`-R`/`--repo` takes a single path. Used alone it points at one jj repo (workspace lookup is
skipped), and combined with `-s` it overrides the workspace root for the role lookup:

```
vc-x1 chid -R .                  # single repo at .
vc-x1 chid -R .claude            # single repo at .claude
vc-x1 chid -R ../other -s work,bot   # both sides of ../other workspace
```

Defaults preserve prior behavior: no flag -> `[.]`, `-R foo` alone -> `[foo]`. When multiple repos
are resolved (any `-s` that names more than one role), output is labeled with bold `=== path ===`
headers by default. Control the label with `-l`/`--label` and `-L`/`--no-label`:

```
vc-x1 chid -s work,agent          # default label: === path ===
vc-x1 chid -s work,bot -l "---"   # custom label:  --- path ---
vc-x1 chid -s work,bot -L         # no label (raw output)
```

Examples:

```
$ vc-x1 chid -s work,bot
=== . ===
kwoyvposvsmv

=== .claude ===
zzpksklxyrnw

$ vc-x1 chid -s work,bot -L
kwoyvposvsmv
zzpksklxyrnw

$ vc-x1 list @.. 3 -s work,bot
=== . ===
kwoyvposvsmv eae175c3c1b5 (no description set)
pqxtxxpnsmot b0c46930a640 Reorganize notes (0.19.1)
ssokyszzwsxw eeb15bc6d839 Unify .. notation and CLI (0.19.0)

=== .claude ===
zzpksklxyrnw 2388185e42ee (no description set)
tzupykyyvnrp 81ce22e34d41 Reorganize notes (0.19.1)
slmkmroqtqtp 1c33ccaa567d Unify .. notation and CLI (0.19.0)

REVISION is `-r`/`--revision` and COMMITS is `-n`/`--commits`, with `..` on either side of the
revision opening that side to the count:

```

vc-x1 list -r ..x.. -n 1       # just x (1 commit)
```

**Defaults:** with no arguments, REVISION is `@` and COMMITS is 1 (just the working copy).

Every argument is a flag: the positionals these commands once took, `list x 5`, are refused, naming
the flag form, `-r x -n 5`.

1	//! CLI subprocess tests for shell completion of path arguments.
2	//!
3	//! The binary answers `COMPLETE=<shell> vc-x1 -- vc-x1 <args>` with
4	//! the candidates for the last argument, which is how the
5	//! `source <(COMPLETE=bash vc-x1)` hook asks. The fish protocol
6	//! prints one candidate per line, so it is the one read here. A
7	//! path argument completes only when clap knows it is one: a
8	//! `PathBuf`, or a `value_hint` on anything else.
9	
10	mod common;
11	
12	use common::{CliFixture, run_ok};
13	
14	/// The candidates the binary offers for the last of `args`, run in
15	/// `dir`.
16	fn complete(fx: &CliFixture, dir: &std::path::Path, args: &[&str]) -> Vec<String> {
17	    let bin = env!("CARGO_PKG_NAME");
18	    let out = run_ok(
19	        fx.cmd()
20	            .current_dir(dir)
21	            .env("COMPLETE", "fish")
22	            .arg("--")
23	            .arg(bin)
24	            .args(args),
25	    );
26	    String::from_utf8_lossy(&out.stdout)
27	        .lines()
28	        .map(|l| l.split('\t').next().unwrap_or(l).to_string()) // OK: split always yields a first piece
29	        .collect()
30	}
31	
32	/// Every argument that takes a path completes one, the ones typed as
33	/// a `String` or parsed by a function of their own included.
34	#[test]
35	fn path_arguments_complete() {
36	    let fx = CliFixture::new("complete-paths");
37	    let dir = fx.path("tree");
38	    std::fs::create_dir_all(dir.join("src")).expect("mkdir src");
39	    std::fs::write(dir.join("notes.md"), "notes\n").expect("write notes");
40	
41	    let cases: &[(&[&str], &str)] = &[
42	        (&["init", "sr"], "src/"),
43	        (&["clone", "sr"], "src/"),
44	        (&["symlink", "sr"], "src/"),
45	        (&["lookup", "no"], "notes.md"),
46	        (&["lookup", "work", "no"], "notes.md"),
47	        (&["init", "x", "--config", "no"], "notes.md"),
48	        (&["init", "x", "--use-template", "sr"], "src/"),
49	        (&["config", "no"], "notes.md"),
50	        (&["validate-config", "no"], "notes.md"),
51	        // Already a `PathBuf`, so it completed before the hints.
52	        (&["validate-anchors", "no"], "notes.md"),
53	    ];
54	    for (args, want) in cases {
55	        let got = complete(&fx, &dir, args);
56	        assert!(
57	            got.iter().any(|c| c == want),
58	            "{args:?} offers {want}: {got:?}"
59	        );
60	    }
61	}

425	### lookup
426	
427	Show the lines in the other repo that a line in this one relates to. `vc-x1 lookup [SCOPE]
428	FILE:LINE` takes a line as an editor, a compiler, or grep prints it, places the file on one side
429	of the workspace, and resolves it to the window on the other side, work-to-transcript or
430	transcript-to-work. The requirements are in [What the lookup command
431	needs](notes/transcript-write.md#what-the-lookup-command-needs).
432	
433	- `SCOPE` is the side the line is on, `work` or `agent`, as a positional before `FILE:LINE` or as
434	  `-s`/`--scope`. Omitted, it is inferred from the file's path. Named, a `FILE` that does not
435	  exist relative to the current directory is taken relative to that side's repo root, so a
436	  repo-relative path works from anywhere once the side is said. A named side the path disagrees
437	  with is an error, never a hint.
438	- `FILE:LINE` splits at its last colon, so a path holding a colon still parses, and the line must
439	  exist in the file on disk.
440	- The workspace is `-R`/`--repo` when given, else found from the file.
441	- `-r`/`--revision REV` reads the line from the file as of REV instead of from disk, for a line
442	  the working copy no longer holds, such as a cycle-record line the next opening deleted.
443	
444	A work line prints the commit it arrived in, blamed at the working copy after a snapshot, and
445	that commit's partner by its `ochid:` trailer. When the line moved, the commit that first wrote
446	it and that commit's partner follow. A commit with no trailer prints its candidate partners, the
447	agent commits within `--tolerance` seconds of it, 60 by default, nearest first:
448	
449	```
450	work TODO.md:21
451	    The first decision needs revising.
452	commit  kxpuoxoznwyn TODO.md:21 fix: the design note closing
453	written yuoqvtxvozko fix: the design note opening
454	partner vxkqvspultnv fix: the design note closing
455	written partner qxqzomnwkonk fix: the design note opening
456	```
457	
458	An agent line, a session file's line, prints as the rendered transcript entry, then the agent
459	commit that appended it, blamed at the agent repo's working copy after a snapshot, and every work
460	commit that commit's `ochid:` trailers name, the work commits its push published. Each work
461	commit's diff is the window, printed as `FILE:START-END` regions with their removed and added
462	lines. When the line is a transcript write the window narrows to the files it wrote, one for a
463	`Write` or `Edit` and every changed file a `Bash` command names, and any other line is discussion
464	and takes the diff whole. A line not yet pushed says so:
465	
466	```
467	agent 1d000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002.jsonl:17
468	    1d000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002.jsonl:17 2026-09-12 20:24:58Z tool Edit: .../dr-1/design.md
469	commit  upzpmzpyuqzo 1d000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002.jsonl:17 fix: revise the first decision
470	partner ntuwppkqupwv fix: revise the first decision
471	write   design.md in ntuwppkqupwv
472	window  design.md:3-3
473	  - The first decision.
474	  + The first decision, revised and checked.
475	```
476

478	vc-x1 lookup TODO.md:53                  # the side inferred from the path
479	vc-x1 lookup agent e355f8b2.jsonl:1200   # repo-relative under the agent repo
480	vc-x1 lookup work TODO.md:53 -R ../proj  # a workspace elsewhere
481	vc-x1 lookup TODO.md:11 -r main-         # the line as of a revision
482	```

### lookup

Show the lines in the other repo that a line in this one relates to. `vc-x1 lookup [SCOPE]
FILE:LINE` takes a line as an editor, a compiler, or grep prints it, places the file on one side
of the workspace, and resolves it to the window on the other side, work-to-transcript or
transcript-to-work. The requirements are in [What the lookup command
needs](notes/transcript-write.md#what-the-lookup-command-needs).

- `SCOPE` is the side the line is on, `work` or `agent`, as a positional before `FILE:LINE` or as
  `-s`/`--scope`. Omitted, it is inferred from the file's path. Named, a `FILE` that does not
  exist relative to the current directory is taken relative to that side's repo root, so a
  repo-relative path works from anywhere once the side is said. A named side the path disagrees
  with is an error, never a hint.
- `FILE:LINE` splits at its last colon, so a path holding a colon still parses, and the line must
  exist in the file on disk.
- The workspace is `-R`/`--repo` when given, else found from the file.
- `-r`/`--revision REV` reads the line from the file as of REV instead of from disk, for a line
  the working copy no longer holds, such as a cycle-record line the next opening deleted.

A work line prints the commit it arrived in, blamed at the working copy after a snapshot, and
that commit's partner by its `ochid:` trailer. When the line moved, the commit that first wrote
it and that commit's partner follow. A commit with no trailer prints its candidate partners, the
agent commits within `--tolerance` seconds of it, 60 by default, nearest first:

```
work TODO.md:21
    The first decision needs revising.
commit  kxpuoxoznwyn TODO.md:21 fix: the design note closing
written yuoqvtxvozko fix: the design note opening
partner vxkqvspultnv fix: the design note closing
written partner qxqzomnwkonk fix: the design note opening
```

An agent line, a session file's line, prints as the rendered transcript entry, then the agent
commit that appended it, blamed at the agent repo's working copy after a snapshot, and every work
commit that commit's `ochid:` trailers name, the work commits its push published. Each work
commit's diff is the window, printed as `FILE:START-END` regions with their removed and added
lines. When the line is a transcript write the window narrows to the files it wrote, one for a
`Write` or `Edit` and every changed file a `Bash` command names, and any other line is discussion
and takes the diff whole. A line not yet pushed says so:

```
agent 1d000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002.jsonl:17
    1d000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002.jsonl:17 2026-09-12 20:24:58Z tool Edit: .../dr-1/design.md
commit  upzpmzpyuqzo 1d000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002.jsonl:17 fix: revise the first decision
partner ntuwppkqupwv fix: revise the first decision
write   design.md in ntuwppkqupwv
window  design.md:3-3
  - The first decision.
  + The first decision, revised and checked.
```

```
vc-x1 lookup TODO.md:53                  # the side inferred from the path
vc-x1 lookup agent e355f8b2.jsonl:1200   # repo-relative under the agent repo
vc-x1 lookup work TODO.md:53 -R ../proj  # a workspace elsewhere
vc-x1 lookup TODO.md:11 -r main-         # the line as of a revision
```

toolUseResult.oldString:
Show the lines in the other repo that a line in this one relates to. `vc-x1 lookup [SCOPE]
FILE:LINE` takes a line as an editor, a compiler, or grep prints it, places the file on one side
of the workspace, and resolves it to the window on the other side, work-to-transcript or
transcript-to-work. The requirements are in [What the lookup command
needs](notes/transcript-write.md#what-the-lookup-command-needs).

- `SCOPE` is the side the line is on, `work` or `agent`, as a positional before `FILE:LINE` or as
  `-s`/`--scope`. Omitted, it is inferred from the file's path. Named, a `FILE` that does not
  exist relative to the current directory is taken relative to that side's repo root, so a
  repo-relative path works from anywhere once the side is said. A named side the path disagrees
  with is an error, never a hint.
- `FILE:LINE` splits at its last colon, so a path holding a colon still parses, and the line must
  exist in the file on disk.

[package]
name = "vc-x1"

# The package name is the installed binary's name and never
# changes: a cycle's validation installs under its own root,
# `--root tmp/dev` in `.vc-config.md`'s `[validate]` lists, so a
# dev build (a suffixed version) never replaces the stable
# `vc-x1` on the PATH. The promotion is the plain `cargo install`
# from `main`. Before 2026-10-20 a cycle renamed the package to
# `vc-x1-dev` instead, guarded by build.rs (chores-16, 0.78.3).

[lints.clippy]
# The process-spawn ban: `Command::new` is disallowed via
# clippy.toml's `disallowed-methods`, and deny (not warn) so a bare
# new spawn site fails `cargo clippy` even without `-D warnings`.
# The documented allowlist lives in clippy.toml.
disallowed_methods = "deny"

[dependencies]
chrono = { version = "0.4", default-features = false, features = ["now"] }
clap = { version = "4.6", features = ["derive", "wrap_help"] }
clap_complete = { version = "4.6", features = ["unstable-dynamic"] }
futures = "0.3"
# The gix jj-lib 0.46 resolves (no features of our own): the
# session's lock-contention downcast needs type identity with the
# errors jj-lib returns, and init's bare-repo creation reuses it.
gix = { version = "0.88", default-features = false }
# When raising jj-lib: check whether it now offers the commits a
# remote's bookmarks are on without fetching. If so, `git_command`
# in src/jj/session.rs and its two callers take it, and

jj-lib = "0.46"
log = { version = "0.4", features = ["std"] }
pollster = "1.0"
# The rng jj-lib's `SecureConfig` takes to mint a repo's config id,

[package]
name = "vc-x1"
version = "0.85.14-3"
edition = "2024"

# The package name is the installed binary's name and never
# changes: a cycle's validation installs under its own root,

# dev build (a suffixed version) never replaces the stable
# `vc-x1` on the PATH. The promotion is the plain `cargo install`
# from `main`. Before 2026-10-20 a cycle renamed the package to
# `vc-x1-dev` instead, guarded by build.rs (chores-16, 0.78.3).

[lints.clippy]
# The process-spawn ban: `Command::new` is disallowed via
# clippy.toml's `disallowed-methods`, and deny (not warn) so a bare
# new spawn site fails `cargo clippy` even without `-D warnings`.
# The documented allowlist lives in clippy.toml.
disallowed_methods = "deny"

[dependencies]
chrono = { version = "0.4", default-features = false, features = ["now"] }
clap = { version = "4.6", features = ["derive", "wrap_help"] }
clap_complete = { version = "4.6", features = ["unstable-dynamic"] }
futures = "0.3"
# The gix jj-lib 0.46 resolves (no features of our own): the

gix = { version = "0.88", default-features = false }
# When raising jj-lib: check whether it now offers the commits a

jj-lib = "0.46"

pollster = "1.0"

# at jj-lib 0.46's versions so the types are its own, seeded the way
# jj-cli seeds it (src/jj/session.rs `load_repo_config`).
rand = "0.10"
rand_chacha = "0.10"
serde_json = "1"

[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]
libc = "0.2"

490	`agent-files version` prints the set version, the name of the `agent-data/agent-files-vX.Y.Z`
491	file with its prefix removed, bare, one per line when a bump left several, and fails outside a
492	workspace or in one without the file.
493	
494	`agent-files diff [A] [B]` compares two copies of the set, one line per file, names only: `same`,
495	`differs`, `only in A`, or `only in B`, then `N of M differ`. It answers whether a re-sync is a
496	copy, and its exit status is non-zero when anything differs, as `diff`'s is. `custom.md` is
497	reported as the project layer and not compared unless `-c`/`--custom` compares it like the rest,
498	for a family whose project layers are meant to be identical, and `--no-custom` overrides a config
499	that says so.
500	
501	`A` is the operand, else the config's `agent-files.diff.dir`, else `family.template`, the config
502	values relative to the config file's directory. `B` is the operand, else this workspace. So a
503	bare `diff` compares the payload against this workspace, one operand compares that copy against
504	this workspace, and two operands compare any two copies from anywhere, no workspace needed. The
505	header line says where each came from, and a missing or non-directory operand is an error naming
506	what to set.
507	
508	`agent-files copy [SRC] [DST]` makes the set in `DST` a byte copy of the one in `SRC`: it copies
509	what differs or exists only in `SRC`, deletes what exists only in `DST` under `agent-data/`,
510	never touches `TODO.md`, and copies `custom.md` only with `-c`/`--custom`. The operands resolve
511	as `diff`'s do: `SRC` is the operand, else `agent-files.copy.dir`, else `family.template`, and
512	`DST` is the operand, else this workspace. So a bare `copy` re-syncs this workspace from the
513	payload, and two operands copy between any two directories, which is how a maintainer folds an
514	adopter's set into the payload. It prints its source and destination and each step first,
515	refuses a `DST` whose jj working copy already changes a set file, so the copy's changes are the
516	only ones there, and leaves the result uncommitted: `jj diff` there is the review, and the
517	commit is yours to make. A `DST` outside any jj repo gets no guard, and the run says so.
518	
519	`agent-files size [DIR]` counts the set's markdown, `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and
520	`agent-data/*.md`, one line per file and a total. The version marker has no `.md` extension, so it
521	takes no row and no place in the file count, and being empty it would add nothing to the total
522	either. `agent-data/rationale.md` is counted: its number is shown in angle brackets and left out
523	of the total, being the rules' why rather than a rule, so a rule gaining a why does not read as
524	the set growing.
525	
526	It then slides the per-file table in `notes/agent-files-size.md`, the one headed `| File |`: a new
527	leftmost column labelled by the set's version file goes in, the rightmost column goes out, and the
528	window keeps the width it had. A file new to the set takes its sorted slot with empty cells behind
529	it, one gone from the set keeps its remaining numbers until the window passes them, and the `total`
530	row stays last. It is dry-run by default, printing the table it would write, and `--no-dry-run`

`agent-files version` prints the set version, the name of the `agent-data/agent-files-vX.Y.Z`
file with its prefix removed, bare, one per line when a bump left several, and fails outside a
workspace or in one without the file.

`agent-files diff [A] [B]` compares two copies of the set, one line per file, names only: `same`,
`differs`, `only in A`, or `only in B`, then `N of M differ`. It answers whether a re-sync is a
copy, and its exit status is non-zero when anything differs, as `diff`'s is. `custom.md` is
reported as the project layer and not compared unless `-c`/`--custom` compares it like the rest,
for a family whose project layers are meant to be identical, and `--no-custom` overrides a config
that says so.

`A` is the operand, else the config's `agent-files.diff.dir`, else `family.template`, the config
values relative to the config file's directory. `B` is the operand, else this workspace. So a
bare `diff` compares the payload against this workspace, one operand compares that copy against
this workspace, and two operands compare any two copies from anywhere, no workspace needed. The
header line says where each came from, and a missing or non-directory operand is an error naming
what to set.

`agent-files copy [SRC] [DST]` makes the set in `DST` a byte copy of the one in `SRC`: it copies
what differs or exists only in `SRC`, deletes what exists only in `DST` under `agent-data/`,
never touches `TODO.md`, and copies `custom.md` only with `-c`/`--custom`. The operands resolve
as `diff`'s do: `SRC` is the operand, else `agent-files.copy.dir`, else `family.template`, and
`DST` is the operand, else this workspace. So a bare `copy` re-syncs this workspace from the
payload, and two operands copy between any two directories, which is how a maintainer folds an
adopter's set into the payload. It prints its source and destination and each step first,
refuses a `DST` whose jj working copy already changes a set file, so the copy's changes are the
only ones there, and leaves the result uncommitted: `jj diff` there is the review, and the
commit is yours to make. A `DST` outside any jj repo gets no guard, and the run says so.

`agent-files size [DIR]` counts the set's markdown, `AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`, and
`agent-data/*.md`, one line per file and a total. The version marker has no `.md` extension, so it
takes no row and no place in the file count, and being empty it would add nothing to the total
either. `agent-data/rationale.md` is counted: its number is shown in angle brackets and left out
of the total, being the rules' why rather than a rule, so a rule gaining a why does not read as
the set growing.

It then slides the per-file table in `notes/agent-files-size.md`, the one headed `| File |`: a new
leftmost column labelled by the set's version file goes in, the rightmost column goes out, and the
window keeps the width it had. A file new to the set takes its sorted slot with empty cells behind
it, one gone from the set keeps its remaining numbers until the window passes them, and the `total`
row stays last. It is dry-run by default, printing the table it would write, and `--no-dry-run`
applies it. `DIR` is the operand, else this workspace, `--file` names another notes file, and
`--label` names a column the version file cannot: write `--label=- v0.1.0` for a label opening on
a `-`. The `## Counts` table above is left alone, since its note is prose.

1478	| `--agent-repo <NAME>` | The agent repo's whole remote name |
1479	| `--agent-suffix <SUFFIX>` | The work repo's name plus this names the agent repo [default: .agent-session] |

1487	**`--use-template`**. Value is `CODE[,BOT]`. If `BOT` is omitted, defaults to the sibling directory
1488	`<CODE>.claude` (file-name concat, not path join, since the two templates are not nested).
1489	Non-hidden contents are copied recursively into each target, and hidden entries (names starting with
1490	`.`) are skipped since init creates the repo's own hidden files (`.vc-config.md`, `.gitignore`,
1491	`.git/`, `.jj/`). If either template has a `README.md` at its root, its first line is rewritten to
1492	`# <repo-name>`: `<name>` for the work repo and `<name>.claude` for the bot repo. For local
1493	verification without hitting GitHub, combine `--use-template` with `--repo local=<PARENT>`.
1494	
1495	**`--adopt`**. Without it an existing TARGET is refused, named by what it holds. With it, init
1496	grows the target into a dual workspace:
1497	
1498	- A plain directory, no repo: both repos are created around it, and everything in it that its
1499	  `.gitignore` does not exclude is the work repo's first commit, whatever the file sizes. Files
1500	  over jj's new-file size limit (1MiB by default) are listed, since jj would otherwise leave them
1501	  out. A `.gitignore` it already has is kept and given the lines it lacks, the agent directory's
1502	  and `/.claude/settings.local.json`.
1503	- A jj repo colocated with git and with no workspace config: its history stays, and one commit,
1504	  "Adopt as a dual-repo workspace", goes on top, carrying `.vc-config.md`, the `.gitignore` lines,
1505	  and the `ochid:` trailer to the agent repo's first commit. With an `origin`, the agent repo's
1506	  remote is derived beside it, `--repo` and `--account` are refused, and the work side pushes
1507	  nothing: the commit is yours to land. With no origin, the remotes come from `--repo` as for a
1508	  fresh init, and both are pushed. A working copy with uncommitted work is refused, and a git-only
1509	  repo is pointed at `jj git init --colocate`.
1510	- A single-repo workspace, one whose config declares `repos.work` alone, such as `init --por`
1511	  makes: adopted as the repo above, except that its config is edited in place. `agent =` goes into
1512	  `[repos]` and `agent-repo =` under `[remote]`, and every other line, prose and comments
1513	  included, stays as it was.
1514	- A dual-repo workspace is refused, having nothing to grow.
1515	
1516	`--adopt` is refused with `--por` and with `--use-template`, and on a TARGET that does not exist.
1517	
1518	Requires `gh` (authenticated) and `jj` to be installed (`gh` is skipped under `--repo local=...`).

```

### clone

Clone an existing dual-repo project. Runs `git clone --recursive` to get both repos, initializes
`jj` in each, and creates the Claude Code symlink.

```
# Clone using a full URL
vc-x1 clone git@github.com:owner/my-project.git
vc-x1 clone https://github.com/owner/my-project

# A slashed source with no path prefix (`owner/my-project`) is
# refused: it reads equally as a path and as the retired owner/name
# shorthand.

# Clone with a custom directory name
vc-x1 clone https://github.com/owner/my-project my-local-name

# Clone into a specific parent directory
vc-x1 clone https://github.com/owner/my-project --dir ~/projects

# Preview without executing
vc-x1 clone https://github.com/owner/my-project --dry-run
```

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `--dir <PATH>` | Parent directory [default: cwd] |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would be done without executing |
| `-v, --verbose` | Verbose output |

Requires `jj` to be installed. The `.claude` bot repo is cloned automatically via `git submodule` if
the source project was created with `vc-x1 init`.

### init

Create a new dual-repo project: a work repo with its agent repo nested inside it, at
`.agent-session` unless `--agent-dir` names another directory. Both repos are initialized with `git`
and `jj`, configured with `.vc-config.md`, and pushed to GitHub. The work repo ignores the agent
repo's directory, and its config records where the agent repo is and what its remote calls it, so
`vc-x1 clone` fetches both.

The agent repo's remote name is the work repo's name plus `.agent-session`, beside the work repo
under the same owner:

- `--agent-suffix` replaces the suffix, and must begin with `.` or `-`.
- `--agent-repo` gives the whole name instead, and the two conflict.
- The directory and the remote name are chosen separately, so `--agent-dir` changes neither name.
- A workspace created before 0.84.12 records no remote name, which reads as `.claude`, the suffix
  init used then.

```
# Create public project in current directory (GitHub via gh)
vc-x1 init my-project

# A URL or a path target. A slashed target with no path prefix
# (`myorg/my-project`) is refused: it reads equally as a path and
# as the retired owner/name shorthand.
vc-x1 init https://github.com/myorg/my-project
vc-x1 init ~/projects/my-project
vc-x1 init ./sub/dir/my-project

# Create private repos
vc-x1 init my-project --private

# Local bare remotes instead of GitHub (offline; used by fixtures)
vc-x1 init my-project --repo local=/path/to/parent

# Preview without executing
vc-x1 init my-project --dry-run

# Grow an existing plain directory into a dual workspace
vc-x1 init . --adopt

# Name the agent repo's directory and its remote
vc-x1 init my-project --agent-dir .sessions --agent-suffix -sessions
vc-x1 init my-project --agent-repo my-project.claude

# Seed both repos from template directories (sibling layout)
vc-x1 init my-project --use-template \
    ../vc-x1-work-repo-template,../vc-x1-bot-repo-template

# BOT omitted defaults to the `<CODE>.claude` sibling
vc-x1 init my-project --use-template ../tmpl
# Equivalent to:
vc-x1 init my-project --use-template ../tmpl,../tmpl.claude
```

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `<TARGET>` | URL, path, or bare NAME |
| `[NAME]` | Repo directory name override (URL form only) |
| `--account <NAME>` | Pick `[account.<a>]` from user config |
| `--repo <CAT[=VAL]>` | Repo target, e.g. `local=<PARENT>` for local bare remotes |
| `--por` | Plain single repo (no agent repo) |
| `--adopt` | Grow an existing TARGET into a dual workspace (see below) |
| `--agent-dir <DIR>` | The agent repo's directory, one name [default: .agent-session] |
| `--agent-repo <NAME>` | The agent repo's whole remote name |
| `--agent-suffix <SUFFIX>` | The work repo's name plus this names the agent repo [default: .agent-session] |
| `--private` | Create private GitHub repos [default: public] |
| `--dry-run` | Show what would be done without executing |
| `--push-retries <N>` | Max push retries after repo creation [default: 5] |
| `--push-retry-delay <N>` | Seconds between push retries [default: 3] |
| `--use-template <CODE[,BOT]>` | Seed both repos from template dirs (see below) |
| `--config <none\|PATH>` | Override the canned config write, under the name the source's carrier calls for |

**`--use-template`**. Value is `CODE[,BOT]`. If `BOT` is omitted, defaults to the sibling directory
`<CODE>.claude` (file-name concat, not path join, since the two templates are not nested).
Non-hidden contents are copied recursively into each target, and hidden entries (names starting with
`.`) are skipped since init creates the repo's own hidden files (`.vc-config.md`, `.gitignore`,
`.git/`, `.jj/`). If either template has a `README.md` at its root, its first line is rewritten to
`# <repo-name>`: `<name>` for the work repo and `<name>.claude` for the bot repo. For local
verification without hitting GitHub, combine `--use-template` with `--repo local=<PARENT>`.

grows the target into a dual workspace:

- A plain directory, no repo: both repos are created around it, and everything in it that its
  `.gitignore` does not exclude is the work repo's first commit, whatever the file sizes. Files

input.new_string:
`init`'s and `clone`'s target and name, and `symlink`'s target, become flags, and `init` and
`clone` take `-s both|por`, `--por` refused naming it, with the account errors and stale help
fixed.

- `init --target URL|PATH|NAME --name NAME`, `clone --from URL|PATH --name NAME`, and `symlink
  --target PATH`, each `--target`/`--from` required unless the retired positionals were given,
  which `retired_positional::refuse_two` refuses, one word or two, and `agent-files diff` now
  shares it.
- `PorFlag` became the creation scope: `-s both|por`, both by default, and `--por` kept hidden as
  `retired_por`, its field name kept apart from the command's `retired`, since clap's argument ids
  must be unique across a flatten. `repo_scope_parser` only hides what it does not offer, so
  `PorFlag::check` refuses `work` and `agent` alone, and `--por`, in each command's `to_params`.
- The `From` conversions stay total, the tests building params from them, `is_por` reading the
  scope and the target unwrapped behind clap's requirement and the refusal before it.
- The dual-only and POR-only errors say `-s por`. The account errors add the URL target as the way
  that needs no config, the user config's path, and the least `[account.<name>]` section.
- Stale help: `init` and `clone` say "a dual workspace or a plain repo with -s por", `--config`
  names `.vc-config.md`, and `--use-template` says `-s por`. The README's `clone` section lost a
  `--dir` flag clone never had and its `git submodule` text, and its `init` section gained the
  `-s por` URL example.
- `support/fixtures/build-dr-1.py` runs `init` against the binary under test, so it names
  `--target`, and the CLI tests and completion cases follow.

186	pub fn install_params(
187	    dev: bool,
188	    repo: Option<&Path>,
189	    dir: Option<&Path>,
190	    dry_run: bool,
191	) -> Result<InstallParams, String> {
192	    let (label, dir_key, list_key) = if dev {
193	        ("install-dev", "install.dev-dir", "install.dev")
194	    } else {
195	        ("install", "install.release-dir", "install.release")
196	    };

198	        (
199	            "build.dev-bin",
200	            &["build.dev-bin", "install.dev-dir", "install.dev-suffix"],
201	        )
202	    } else {
203	        (
204	            "build.release-bin",
205	            &["build.release-bin", "install.release-dir"],
206	        )
207	    };
208	    let root = match repo {
209	        Some(p) => crate::common::find_workspace_root_from(p)
210	            .ok_or_else(|| format!("{label}: '{}' is not in a vc-x1 workspace", p.display()))?,
211	        None => crate::common::find_workspace_root()
212	            .ok_or_else(|| format!("{label}: not in a vc-x1 workspace (no config found)"))?,
213	    };
214	    let dest_dir = dest_dir(&root, dir, dir_key).map_err(|e| format!("{label}: {e}"))?;
215	    let build = build_params(dev, Some(&root))?;
216	    let bin = if dev {

219	        release_bin(&root)?
220	    };
221	    let suffix = if dev {
