        the binary already tested is the one copied. The build leaves the\n\
        release at `[build] release-bin` (here `target/release/vc-x1`), and\n\
        `install` copies it into the one directory `[install] release-dir`\n\
        names (here `~/.cargo/bin`, `~` expanded), under the same file name.\n\
        It does not search $PATH. The copy goes to a temporary file renamed\n\
        into place, so a running copy of the old binary is undisturbed and a\n\
        failed copy leaves the old one. An `[install] release` list, when\n\
        present, runs in place of the copy, each word's {build.release-bin}\n\
        and {install.release-dir} filled with the values resolved for the\n\
        run, --dir applied, so the list names every path it writes. This\n\
        workspace's list is the copy written out.\n\n\

README.md:100:  cycle's code can be tried from any directory ([install-dev](#install-dev)). With `install`, the
README.md:1041:[install-dev](#install-dev) copies it.
### build

Build the workspace's release with `build`, or its dev build with `build --dev`, by the work side's
`[build]` table (see [Workspace config tables](#workspace-config-tables)). The lists run as
[validate](#validate)'s do: each element one command, split on whitespace with no shell in between,
run in order from the work repo root, the first failure stopping the run. Neither touches the PATH,
which is `vc-x1 install`'s.

- `vc-x1 build` runs `[build] release`, which builds the release, and then checks it left
  `[build] release-bin`.
- `vc-x1 build --dev` runs `[build] dev`, the dev build. A command per build, named with the `-dev`
  suffix as `run` and `run --dev` are.
- Neither tracks whether its binary is out of date: cargo does, rebuilding only what changed, so
  a build with nothing changed is quick and leaves the binary as it was.
- Both commands run their lists with two variables added to the environment,
  `VC_X1_BUILD_COMMIT`, the full commit id of `@-`, and `VC_X1_BUILD_STATE`, `clean` or `dirty`,
  so an artifact that compiles them in can say what it was built from wherever it is copied.
  `validate` passes the same two, so the test build it leaves has the same values and
  `build --dev` reuses it rather than recompiling. vc-x1 compiles them in, as semver build metadata
  in its banner, and as a `build` line in `vc-x1 version`:

| `--dir <DIR>` | Copy into `DIR` instead of `[install] release-dir`, for this run |
| `-R, --repo <DIR>` | Workspace to install from [default: the one containing the current directory] |

### install-dev

Build the dev build, then copy it into the install directory with `[install] dev-suffix`, `-dev`
when absent, appended to its file name. It first runs `[build] dev` exactly as [build-dev](#build)
does, then copies `[build] dev-bin`, `target/debug/vc-x1` here, into the directory `[install]
dev-dir` or `--dir` names, as `vc-x1-dev`. The landed `vc-x1` and the cycle's `vc-x1-dev` then sit
side by side on the PATH, so the dev build can be tried from any directory, another project's
included, where `vc-x1 run --dev` would run that project's dev build instead. The suffix is what lets
`dev-dir` be `release-dir`'s own directory, the dev build beside the release without replacing it,
and without a list `install --dev` refuses before the build when its destination would be the
release's, as an empty suffix in that directory or a `--dir` onto it would make it. A list writes
where it says, so it names the suffix itself, `{install.dev-suffix}`, as this workspace's does.

The report, the refusals, the copy, `--dry-run`, and `--dir` are [install](#install)'s, the binary
being the dev build's, and an `[install] dev` list runs in place of the copy as `[install] release`
does for `install`, its placeholders `{build.dev-bin}` and `{install.dev-dir}`. With a list the
`-dev` name is the list's to write, as this workspace's does: a list that left it off would write
the release's name and, with `dev-dir` the release's own directory, replace the release.

```
# Mid-cycle: put the rung's code on the PATH as vc-x1-dev, and try it in another project
vc-x1 install --dev
cd ../other-project
vc-x1-dev status
```

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `--dry-run` | Build and report, and copy nothing |
| `--dir <DIR>` | Copy into `DIR` instead of `[install] dev-dir`, for this run |
| `-R, --repo <DIR>` | Workspace to install from [default: the one containing the current directory] |

### run and run-dev

Build, then run the build's binary with the given arguments, as `cargo run` builds before it runs.
`vc-x1 run` runs `[build] release` exactly as [build](#build) does, then `[build] release-bin`,
and `vc-x1 run --dev` runs `[build] dev`, then `[build] dev-bin`, so what runs is always the current
code. Neither touches the PATH, so a build is tried before [install](#install) or
[install-dev](#install-dev) copies it.

- The arguments go to the binary untouched. One that starts with `-` comes after `--`, as with
  `cargo run`, since vc-x1's own flags are read first: `vc-x1 run -V` prints vc-x1's banner,
  and `vc-x1 run -- -V` runs the release's `-V`.
- The binary runs in the current directory, with the terminal, and its exit code is vc-x1's, so
  a failing run fails the same way.
- Before it runs, its `-V` is read, and a version other than the manifest's is a warning naming
  the key: the build passed but left an older binary where the config says. A binary whose `-V`
  prints no version, another project's, is run without the check.
- `--dry-run` prints the build's list and the command, and runs nothing.
- Completion is the binary's own: `vc-x1 run --dev <words><TAB>` asks the dev build, in clap's
  completion mode, to complete `<words>`, so in iiac-perf `vc-x1 run --dev run <TAB>` offers its
  benches. The binary is asked as it stands, never built, and one that is not there, or answers
  nothing, offers nothing. A binary built with clap's dynamic completion answers; another offers
  nothing.

```
# The smoke check before install: build the release and print its version
vc-x1 run -- -V

# Try the rung's code: build the dev build and run its status
vc-x1 run --dev status -s b

# See what would run
vc-x1 run --dev --dry-run status -s b
```

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|

### Every argument is a flag

Every argument is a flag, the command names aside, so a word on the command line says what it is
and never reads two ways by its place: in `push -s b feature`, `feature` could have been the
bookmark to move or the commit it is at, and `push -s b --bookmark feature` is one of them. The
command line is also what is reviewed before a write runs, and a flag says what each word means.
The same names mean the same thing everywhere:

| Flag | Means |
|------|-------|
| `-s, --scope` | Which repos: `w\|work`, `a\|agent`, `b\|both`, or `p\|por` |
| `-R, --repo` | Where: a path in the workspace, or a plain repo |
| `-r, --revision` | A revision, as jj resolves it, `..` notation on the read commands |
| `-n, --commits` | How many commits a read command shows |
| `--bookmark` | A bookmark's name, the one to move or a new one to create |
| `--file`, `--dir` | A file or a directory a command reads |
| `-d, --dev` | The dev build, on `build`, `install`, and `run` |

The one exception is `run`'s trailing arguments, which are the built binary's, not vc-x1's.

A positional a command once took is kept hidden and refused, naming the flag that replaced it with
the value in place, so a stale doc or a habit is told its own fix:

```
$ vc-x1 push -s b @-
error: push: the positional is retired, every argument is a flag: `-r @-`
```

`build-dev`, `install-dev`, and `run-dev` are refused the same way, naming `build --dev`, `install
--dev`, and `run --dev`, and `init --por` and `clone --por` name `--scope por`.

Every argument is a flag, the command names aside, so a word on the command line says what it is
and never reads two ways by its place: in `push -s b feature`, `feature` could have been the
bookmark to move or the commit it is at, and `push -s b --bookmark feature` is one of them. The

The same names mean the same thing everywhere:

| Flag | Means |
|------|-------|
| `-s, --scope` | Which repos: `w\|work`, `a\|agent`, `b\|both`, or `p\|por` |

| `-r, --revision` | A revision, as jj resolves it, `..` notation on the read commands |
| `-n, --commits` | How many commits a read command shows |

| `--file`, `--dir` | A file or a directory a command reads |
| `-d, --dev` | The dev build, on `build`, `install`, and `run` |

The one exception is `run`'s trailing arguments, which are the built binary's, not vc-x1's.

A positional a command once took is kept hidden and refused, naming the flag that replaced it with
the value in place, so a stale doc or a habit is told its own fix:

error: push: the positional is retired, every argument is a flag: `-r @-`
```

`build-dev`, `install-dev`, and `run-dev` are refused the same way, naming `build --dev`, `install
--dev`, and `run --dev`, and `init --por` and `clone --por` name `--scope por`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage: hooks.sh check|install|test
#
# The Claude Code hooks the agent-files carry, beside this script, installed into
# ~/.claude/hooks and registered in ~/.claude/settings.json (AGENTS.md > Working practices).
#
#   check    each hook installed identical to this copy and registered, else what is not, exit 1
#   install  copy the hooks in and register what is missing, the settings file backed up first
#   test     run bash-guard.sh over commands it must deny or allow
#
# HOOKS_DIR and SETTINGS override the two destinations, for trying install somewhere harmless.
set -euo pipefail
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
dest=${HOOKS_DIR:-$HOME/.claude/hooks}
settings=${SETTINGS:-$HOME/.claude/settings.json}
# How a registration names its script: the ~ form settings.json already uses, or the override.
cmd_dir=${HOOKS_DIR:-'~/.claude/hooks'}

scripts=(bash-allow.sh bash-guard.sh inhibit-sleep.sh)

# One registration per line: event, matcher (empty for none), command.
registrations() {
  cat <<EOF
UserPromptSubmit||$cmd_dir/inhibit-sleep.sh start
SubagentStart||$cmd_dir/inhibit-sleep.sh sub-start
SubagentStop||$cmd_dir/inhibit-sleep.sh sub-stop
Stop||$cmd_dir/inhibit-sleep.sh stop
SessionEnd||$cmd_dir/inhibit-sleep.sh end
PreToolUse|Bash|$cmd_dir/bash-allow.sh
PreToolUse|Bash|$cmd_dir/bash-guard.sh
EOF
}

registered() { # event matcher command
  [[ -f $settings ]] || return 1
  jq -e --arg e "$1" --arg m "$2" --arg c "$3" \
    '(.hooks[$e] // []) | any(.[]; (.matcher // "") == $m and any(.hooks[]?; .command == $c))' \
    "$settings" >/dev/null
}

check() {
  local bad=0 s e m c
  for s in "${scripts[@]}"; do
    if [[ ! -f $dest/$s ]]; then
      echo "hooks: missing    $dest/$s"
      bad=1
    elif ! cmp -s "$here/$s" "$dest/$s"; then
      echo "hooks: differs    $dest/$s"
      bad=1
    fi
  done
  while IFS='|' read -r e m c; do
    if ! registered "$e" "$m" "$c"; then
      echo "hooks: unregistered $e${m:+ [$m]}: $c"
      bad=1
    fi
  done < <(registrations)
  if ((bad)); then
    echo "hooks: not installed, run: bash $here/hooks.sh install"
    return 1
  fi
  echo "hooks: ${#scripts[@]} hooks installed and registered"
}

install() {
  local s e m c tmp
  mkdir -p "$dest"
  for s in "${scripts[@]}"; do
    if ! cmp -s "$here/$s" "$dest/$s" 2>/dev/null; then
      cp "$here/$s" "$dest/$s.new"
      chmod +x "$dest/$s.new"
      mv "$dest/$s.new" "$dest/$s"
      echo "hooks: installed  $dest/$s"
    fi
  done
  [[ -f $settings ]] || echo '{}' >"$settings"
  local backed_up=0
  while IFS='|' read -r e m c; do
    registered "$e" "$m" "$c" && continue
    if ((!backed_up)); then
      cp "$settings" "$settings.$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).bak"
      backed_up=1
    fi
    tmp=$(mktemp "$settings.XXXXXX")
    jq --arg e "$e" --arg m "$m" --arg c "$c" '
      {type: "command", command: $c} as $h
      | .hooks //= {} | .hooks[$e] //= []
      | if any(.hooks[$e][]; (.matcher // "") == $m)
        then .hooks[$e] |= map(if (.matcher // "") == $m then .hooks += [$h] else . end)
        else .hooks[$e] += [(if $m == "" then {} else {matcher: $m} end) + {hooks: [$h]}]
        end' "$settings" >"$tmp"
    mv "$tmp" "$settings"
    echo "hooks: registered $e${m:+ [$m]}: $c"
  done < <(registrations)
  check
}

# Each case: the decision bash-guard.sh must make, then the command.
guard_cases() {
  cat <<'EOF'
deny|false; echo rc=$?
deny|vc-x1-dev install-dev 2>&1 | tail -4; echo rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
deny|cargo test 2>&1 | tail -3
deny|cargo test | tail -3; exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]}
deny|cd /home/me/vc-x1; vc-x1 validate | grep FAILED
deny|tmp/candidate/vc-x1 land -s b --dry-run | head
allow|jq -n 1 | grep 1
allow|cargo --version || { rc=$?; echo failed=$rc; exit $rc; }
allow|set -o pipefail; cargo test 2>&1 | tail -3
allow|cd /home/me/vc-x1; jq . f.json | grep x
allow|cargo test -- --include-ignored
allow|vc-x1 validate
allow|echo done
EOF
}

test_guard() {
  local want cmd out got fail=0 n=0
  while IFS='|' read -r want cmd; do
    out=$(jq -n --arg c "$cmd" '{tool_name: "Bash", tool_input: {command: $c}}' |
      bash "$here/bash-guard.sh")
    got=allow
    if [[ -n $out ]]; then
      got=$(jq -r '.hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision' <<<"$out")
    fi
    n=$((n + 1))
    if [[ $got != "$want" ]]; then
      echo "hooks: FAIL want $want, got $got: $cmd"
      fail=1
    fi
  done < <(guard_cases)
  if ((fail)); then
    return 1
  fi
  echo "hooks: bash-guard.sh passed $n cases"
}

case "${1:-}" in
  check) check ;;
  install) install ;;
  test) test_guard ;;
  *)
    echo "usage: hooks.sh check|install|test" >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac

# Agent-files size

The line count of the agent-files, one row per landing that changed them, so the set's size is
tracked over time. A cycle that leaves the agent-files untouched adds no row, since a row saying
the count did not move records nothing. Smaller is the quasi-goal: a rule stated once is shorter
than a rule stated three times, and a shrinking count is evidence the set is converging, while a
growing one is a prompt to ask what arrived as a paragraph that should have been a line. The count
is not a rule, and a rule is never cut to move it.

A finding from the proposal cycle (2026-08-27), for whoever next tries a cut: a draft that cut

## In Progress

### feat: install --dev --release soaks a release candidate

Picked from `## Todo` as **install --dev --release soaks a release candidate** (wink + agent,
2026-10-27), deferred from **feat: build, install, and run take --dev**, in the cycle **feat: the
other commands take flags only**. The first cycle run in the v0.3.1 form, wink's call (2026-10-27):
a single-step cycle begins with `commit --opening`, its work squashed into that commit, the commit
bodies two paragraphs, the problem and "Solution:", ladder labels from `[0]`, and the continuation
notes in the closing.

#### Problem

`--dev` names the binary `<name>-dev` and chooses the dev build, one flag for both, so a release
build cannot be installed under the dev name for a period of use beside the landed one. The
config is the obstacle: `[install] dev` names its binary `{build.dev-bin}`, so the dev list with
the release build would copy the debug binary.

#### Solution

- `install --dev --release`: `--release` chooses the release profile, the build and its binary,
  and `--dev` the name, the directory, the suffix, and the list. `--release` is install's alone and
  requires `--dev`, the release being the default otherwise.
- `{build.bin}`, a profile-neutral placeholder offered to every install list, the binary of the
  build that ran. A list may name its profile's own key too, and the other profile's is not
  offered, so a dev list naming `{build.dev-bin}` under `--release` is refused before the build,
  the refusal naming `{build.bin}`.
- This workspace's `[install]` lists move to `{build.bin}`, and `vc-x1-config`'s schema prose, the
  model, the README's install section, and the help say so.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with tests that `install --dev --release` resolves the release build and its
binary with the dev directory, suffix, and list, that a dev list naming `{build.dev-bin}` is refused
under `--release` naming `{build.bin}`, and that `--release` without `--dev` is refused. Live:
`vc-x1-dev install --dev --release --dir tmp/soak` builds the release and installs it as
`tmp/soak/vc-x1-dev`, which `cmp` finds identical to `target/release/vc-x1`, and whose `-V` names
this cycle's version.

#### Deliberation

- Single-step, by the v0.3.1 rule that a cycle's shape is its branch's commit count: one feature in
  one module, its config, and its docs.
- `--release` on install alone: `build` and `run` choose a build and no name, so `--release` there
  would only undo `--dev`.
- `{build.bin}` beside the profile keys rather than in place of them: a list naming its own
  profile's key keeps working, and one naming the other profile's is caught, not run.

#### Ladder

- feat: install --dev --release soaks a release candidate (current)

content.text:
**What "soak" means:** to soak a release candidate is to install the build you intend to release and use it day to day for a while before landing it, so problems that only show up in real use surface first. The term comes from soak testing, which runs something under normal load for a long time. Here it would mean the release build installed as `vc-x1-dev` next to the landed `vc-x1`, so you can live with it before it replaces the real one.

**`--profile` instead of `--release`:** that's a better generalization. One thing to settle first: vc-x1 doesn't run cargo itself. It runs the build commands listed in `.vc-config.md` and finds the binary where the config says, `release-bin` or `dev-bin`, on purpose, so vc-x1 "never works it out from cargo or the package's name". So a profile has to be something the config names. Checking whether the schema already allows keys it doesn't list, like a custom profile name would need:

content.text:
The schema already allows keys it doesn't list: a quoted segment like `[repo.category."<cat>"]` stands for any name. So a profile can be any name the config gives it. The proposed design:

**Profiles are named by `[build]` keys.** `release` and `dev` already follow this pattern: `[build] release` is the command list and `release-bin` the binary it leaves. A custom profile is two more keys with any name:

```toml
[build]
release = ["cargo build --release --locked"]
release-bin = "target/release/vc-x1"
dev = ["cargo build --locked"]
dev-bin = "target/debug/vc-x1"
release-lto = ["cargo build --profile release-lto --locked"]   # a custom cargo profile
release-lto-bin = "target/release-lto/vc-x1"
```

The schema gains two dynamic keys, `[build."<profile>"]` and `[build."<profile>-bin"]`. Nothing existing has to change, and vc-x1 still never works out cargo's paths itself.

**The flags:**
- **`--profile NAME`** on `build`, `run`, and `install` chooses which build runs and which binary is used: `[build] NAME` and `NAME-bin`. The default is `release`, or `dev` with `--dev`.
- **On `build` and `run`**, `--dev` stays as shorthand for `--profile dev`. Giving both is refused, since they would both be choosing the build.
- **On `install`**, the two compose: `--dev` chooses the name, `vc-x1-dev`, along with its directory, suffix, and `[install] dev` list, and `--profile` chooses the build.
  - `install --dev --profile release` is the soak.
  - `install --dev --profile release-lto` soaks a custom profile.
  - `install --profile release-lto` installs it as the plain `vc-x1`.
- **`{build.bin}`** stays the profile-neutral placeholder, so install lists work with any profile. The profile-specific keys still work, but only for their own profile.
- **A profile with no `[build] NAME`** is refused before anything runs, and the error names the two keys to add.

The cycle title becomes **feat: build, install, and run take --profile**. Is that the design you want? Two open choices:
1. Should a custom profile live as two keys in `[build]`, as above, or in a table of its own, such as `[build.profile.<name>]` with `commands` and `bin` entries?
2. On `build` and `run`, should `--dev` remain as shorthand for `--profile dev`?

content.text:
Yes, I think that's better. It mirrors cargo, which has one build command and a `--profile` that picks the profile, instead of a list per profile. Here's how I read your suggestion:

```toml
[profile]
release = "release"        # profile name = the directory cargo builds it into, under target/
dev = "debug"              # cargo's one irregular case: profile dev builds into target/debug
release-lto = "release-lto"

[build]
commands = ["cargo build --profile {profile} --locked"]
bin = "target/{profile.dir}/vc-x1"
```

- **`[profile]`** lists the profiles the workspace builds. Each key is a profile name and its value is the directory cargo leaves that build in. The config states the `dev` → `debug` mapping, so vc-x1 still never derives cargo's paths itself.
- **Substitution:** `{profile}` is the chosen name and `{profile.dir}` its directory, filled into `[build] commands` and `bin` the same way install lists already fill `{build.release-bin}`. One build list and one binary pattern cover every profile. Adding a profile is one line in `[profile]`, and `cargo build --profile dev` and `--profile release` both work, so `release` and `dev` need no special case.
- **The flags:** `--profile NAME` on `build`, `run`, and `install`, defaulting to `release`. A name not in `[profile]` is refused, and the error lists the ones that are.
  - On `build` and `run`, `--dev` is shorthand for `--profile dev`.
  - On `install`, `--dev` chooses the name (`vc-x1-dev`, plus its directory, suffix, and `[install] dev` list), and `--profile` chooses the build, so `install --dev --profile release` is the soak.
- **Install lists** use `{build.bin}`, the binary filled in for the chosen profile.

**What it costs:**
- **One command list for every profile.** A project whose dev build needs a different step can't say so any more. I'd allow an optional `[build] "<profile>"` list that overrides `commands` for that one profile, so that need still has a home.
- **A schema change for every adopter.** `[build] release`, `dev`, `release-bin`, and `dev-bin` retire. I'd move this workspace to the new shape in this cycle. For adopters, `validate-config` would name the old keys and the new form, and the old keys would keep working until one of them adopts the change, so nothing breaks unannounced.

The cycle would be **feat: build, install, and run take --profile**. That's no longer one straightforward step: it touches the schema, `build`, `run`, `install`, and the migration. So I'd make it a multi-step ladder rather than single-step.

content.text:
I like the direction: a profile becomes the one thing that names a build, and `--dev` goes away. I'd change two things in your sketch.

**1. Named properties, not positions.** `{profile.release[2]}` only works if you remember that index 2 is the binary for release, while for dev the binary is index 1. The meaning lives in the position, and it differs between profiles. Named keys say what each value is:

```toml
[profile.release]
flags = ["--release"]
bin = "target/release/vc-x1"
suffix = ""

[profile.dev]
flags = []
bin = "target/debug/vc-x1"
suffix = "-dev"
```

**2. Then `[build]` and `[install]` need one list each, not one per profile.** `{profile.X}` means the profile `--profile` chose, so the per-profile keys in your `[build]` disappear:

```toml
[build]
commands = ["cargo build {profile.flags} --locked"]

[install]
dir = "~/.cargo/bin"
commands = [
  "cp {profile.bin} {install.dir}/vc-x1{profile.suffix}.new",
  "mv {install.dir}/vc-x1{profile.suffix}.new {install.dir}/vc-x1{profile.suffix}",
]
```

**What falls out of it:**
- **`--dev` isn't needed.** `install --profile dev` installs `vc-x1-dev` because the dev profile's suffix is `-dev`, and `build`/`run --profile dev` build and run it. `--dev` would be refused, naming `--profile dev`, the same treatment the positionals got.
- **A soak is just another profile.** No composing of two flags:
  ```toml
  [profile.rc]
  flags = ["--release"]
  bin = "target/release/vc-x1"
  suffix = "-rc"
  ```
  `install --profile rc` puts the release build on the PATH as `vc-x1-rc`, beside `vc-x1` and `vc-x1-dev`. A custom cargo profile is the same: `flags = ["--profile", "release-lto"]`.
- **The default** is `release` when `--profile` is left out, or a `[build] default-profile` key if you'd rather the config say it.

**One mechanical detail:** dev's `flags` is empty. Today a list is split into words before placeholders are filled, so an empty value would leave an empty argument, and cargo rejects that. So a list-valued property like `flags` would expand to zero or more words where it appears. That's a small change to the placeholder filling, and it's what makes `{profile.flags}` work for both profiles.

**What it costs:**
- **Every adopter's config changes.** `[build] release`, `dev`, `release-bin`, `dev-bin`, and `[install] release`, `dev`, `release-dir`, `dev-dir`, `dev-suffix` all retire. I'd have `validate-config` name the old keys and show the new form.
- **`--dev`, added in the last cycle, retires again**, one day after landing.

It's clearly a multi-step cycle: the placeholder expansion, the profile schema, `build`/`run`/`install`, retiring the old keys, and the docs and agent-files. The title would be **feat: build, install, and run take --profile**.

### feat: build, install, and run take --profile

Picked from `## Todo` as **install --dev --release soaks a release candidate** (wink + agent,
2026-10-27), deferred from **feat: build, install, and run take --dev**, and widened at its
opening's review into named build profiles, `--profile` replacing `--dev` (wink + agent,
2026-10-27). The first cycle run in the v0.3.1 form, wink's call (2026-10-27): it begins with
`commit --opening`, its commit bodies are two paragraphs, the problem and "Solution:", its ladder
labels count from `[0]`, and its continuation notes go in the closing.

#### Problem

A build is chosen by two fixed names, `release` and `dev`, each with its own keys in `[build]` and
`[install]`, and `--dev` chooses the dev build and the `-dev` name at once. So no other build can be
made, a custom `Cargo.toml` profile included, and a release build cannot be installed under another
name for a period of use beside the landed one, a soak: the `[install] dev` list names
`{build.dev-bin}`, so the dev list with the release build would copy the debug binary.

#### Solution

- A profile is a `[profile.<name>]` table of properties, any name and any properties. vc-x1 reads
  two itself, `bin`, the binary the build leaves, and `suffix`, appended to the installed name, ""
  when absent. The rest are the lists' to use.
- `build`, `run`, and `install` take `--profile NAME`, and `{profile.<property>}` in `[build]
  commands` and `[install] commands` is the chosen profile's property, so one build list and one
  install list serve every profile. The default profile is `[build] default-profile`, else
  `release`, and a name with no table is refused naming the tables there are.
- The encouraged form is a `Cargo.toml` profile, named by the `cargo` property: `cargo build
  --profile {profile.cargo} --locked`, cargo's `dev` and `release` and any custom one alike. A
  list-valued property such as `flags = ["--release"]` expands to its words where it is named, none
  for an empty list, so a build by flags works too.
- `release` and `dev` are examples the generated config and the model carry, `dev` with suffix
  `-dev`, and a soak is one more profile, the release build with its own suffix.
- `--dev` is retired, refused naming `--profile dev`, and the old keys, `[build] release`, `dev`,
  `release-bin`, `dev-bin`, and `[install] release`, `dev`, `release-dir`, `dev-dir`, `dev-suffix`,
  are reported by `validate-config` and refused by the commands, each naming the profile form. This
  workspace's config moves to it.
- The README, the help, `vc-config.md` and its model, `init`'s generated config, and the
  agent-files' `install --dev` say `--profile`, the last told to **agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1**.

  - `command_list::expand` takes list values beside the string ones: a word that is `{name}` alone,
    for a list, becomes the list's items, one word each, none for an empty one.
  - `words` stays, the strings-only form, delegating to `expand`, so its callers are unchanged until
    the profile rung passes lists.
* A list inside a longer word, `x{flags}`, has no word for its items to share.
  - It is refused, naming the list and the word, rather than joined with a guessed separator.
* The refusal for an unknown name offered the string placeholders alone.
  - It offers the lists too, so a typo is told every name the list may use.

## build.release

The release build: the commands that build the artifact, in order, each element one invocation whose
exit status is checked, leaving the binary where it can be run before anything on the PATH is
replaced, `target/release` for a plain `cargo build --release`. `vc-x1 build` runs it from any
commit, and checks it left [build.release-bin](#buildrelease-bin). `vc-x1 run` runs it before it
runs the binary, and `vc-x1 install` before it copies the binary at a cycle's Land. Its commands
run with `VC_X1_BUILD_COMMIT` and `VC_X1_BUILD_STATE` in their environment, the same facts, for an
artifact that compiles them in, as [build.dev](#builddev)'s and the `[validate]` lists' do. Owned by
the work side because it builds the artifact.

```toml
[build.release]
homes = ["workspace-code"]
kind = "str-list"
doc = "The release build, in order, one invocation per element, run by `vc-x1 build`"
used-by = "vc-x1 build, vc-x1 run, and vc-x1 install"
example = ["cargo build --release --locked"]
```

## build.release-bin

The binary the release build leaves, relative to the config file's directory, or as is when
absolute. vc-x1 never works it out, from cargo or from the package's name: the release build's
commands decide where the binary goes, so the config says. `vc-x1 build` checks the build left it,
`vc-x1 run` runs it with the arguments given and warns when its `-V` is not the manifest's version,
and `vc-x1 install` copies it and reports what its `-V` says. Required by `vc-x1 build`, `vc-x1
run`, and `vc-x1 install`.

```toml
[build.release-bin]
homes = ["workspace-code"]
kind = "str"
doc = "The release build's binary, run by `vc-x1 run` and copied by `vc-x1 install`"
used-by = "vc-x1 build, vc-x1 run, and vc-x1 install"
example = "target/release/vc-x1"
```

`{profile.<property>}` filled from the chosen profile and `{install.dir}` from

`{profile.bin}` and the installed name's ending as `{profile.suffix}`. Absent, the built-in copy
puts `{profile.bin}` in `{install.dir}` under its file name with the suffix appended.

'''

finished cycle's is in [zCLOSED.md](zCLOSED.md), and what we might do is in [TODO.md](TODO.md). The
block's shape is on trial: it opens with the Todo as it was picked from `TODO.md`, then the
Deliberation, the plan, Solution and Acceptance check, and the Ladder with its details.

This file is a trial (2026-10-09). The agent-files still name `TODO.md > ## In Progress` as the
record's home, and the cycle that makes this file the rule is [The cycle-record moves out of
TODO.md into zDOING.md](TODO.md#the-cycle-record-moves-out-of-todomd-into-zdoingmd).

## Continuation notes

Where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a record: read first, acted
on, and reset to `_None._` by the reader. Kept here by the trial and no longer in `TODO.md`,
where [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint) still says to look.

## In Progress

### feat: build, install, and run take --profile

Picked from `## Todo` as **install --dev --release soaks a release candidate** (wink + agent,
2026-10-27), deferred from **feat: build, install, and run take --dev**, and widened at its
opening's review into named build profiles, `--profile` replacing `--dev` (wink + agent,
2026-10-27). The first cycle run in the v0.3.1 form, wink's call (2026-10-27): it begins with
`commit --opening`, its commit bodies are two paragraphs, the problem and "Solution:", its ladder
labels count from `[0]`, and its continuation notes go in the closing.

#### Problem

A build is chosen by two fixed names, `release` and `dev`, each with its own keys in `[build]` and
`[install]`, and `--dev` chooses the dev build and the `-dev` name at once. So no other build can be
made, a custom `Cargo.toml` profile included, and a release build cannot be installed under another
name for a period of use beside the landed one, a soak: the `[install] dev` list names
`{build.dev-bin}`, so the dev list with the release build would copy the debug binary.

#### Solution

- A profile is a `[profile.<name>]` table of properties, any name and any properties. vc-x1 reads
  two itself, `bin`, the binary the build leaves, and `suffix`, appended to the installed name, ""
  when absent. The rest are the lists' to use.
- `build`, `run`, and `install` take `--profile NAME`, and `{profile.<property>}` in `[build]
  commands` and `[install] commands` is the chosen profile's property, so one build list and one
  install list serve every profile. The default profile is `[build] default-profile`, else
  `release`, and a name with no table is refused naming the tables there are.
- The encouraged form is a `Cargo.toml` profile, named by the `cargo` property: `cargo build
  --profile {profile.cargo} --locked`, cargo's `dev` and `release` and any custom one alike. A
  list-valued property such as `flags = ["--release"]` expands to its words where it is named, none
  for an empty list, so a build by flags works too.
- `release` and `dev` are examples the generated config and the model carry, `dev` with suffix
  `-dev`, and a soak is one more profile, the release build with its own suffix.
- `--dev` is retired, refused naming `--profile dev`, and the old keys, `[build] release`, `dev`,
  `release-bin`, `dev-bin`, and `[install] release`, `dev`, `release-dir`, `dev-dir`, `dev-suffix`,
  are reported by `validate-config` and refused by the commands, each naming the profile form. This
  workspace's config moves to it.
- The README, the help, `vc-config.md` and its model, `init`'s generated config, and the
  agent-files' `install --dev` say `--profile`, the last told to **agent-files(proposal): v0.3.1**.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with tests that a list-valued placeholder expands to its words, that
`--profile` chooses the profile's properties for `build`, `run`, and `install`, that an unknown
profile and `--dev` are refused naming the fix, and that `validate-config` reports the old keys.
Live, from the rung that lands `--profile` on: `vc-x1-dev install --profile dev` installs
`vc-x1-dev`, `vc-x1-dev run --profile dev -- -V` prints the dev build's banner, and `vc-x1-dev
install --profile rc --dir tmp/soak`, with a `[profile.rc]` building `release` under suffix `-rc`,
installs `tmp/soak/vc-x1-rc`, which `cmp` finds identical to `target/release/vc-x1`.

#### Deliberation

- Named profiles over a `--release` beside `--dev`, wink's call at the opening's review
  (2026-10-27): a profile names the build and the installed name together, so a soak is a profile
  and not two flags composed, and any build can be made, a custom `Cargo.toml` profile included.
- Named properties over positions, the agent's suggestion taken (2026-10-27): wink's sketch,
  `release = ["--release", "--locked", "target/release/vc-x1"]` read as `{profile.release[2]}`,
  put the meaning in the index, which differed between profiles.
- One `[build] commands` and one `[install] commands` filled from the chosen profile, rather than a
  list per profile, since `{profile.<property>}` is the chosen profile's.
- `Cargo.toml` profiles encouraged, wink's call (2026-10-27), read as a `cargo` property naming the
  profile, "simpler" since cargo then owns the flags and the directory: wink wrote
  `{profile.full}` with `[profile].full = "xyz"`, and the name `cargo` is the agent's, provisional.
  The flags form works too.
- `release` and `dev` are examples, not built in, wink's call (2026-10-27): any profile can be
  built. The default when `--profile` is left out is provisional, `[build] default-profile`, else
  `release`.
- A list-valued property expands to words, since lists are split before they are filled and an
  empty value would otherwise be an empty argument cargo refuses.
- The old keys are refused, not kept working beside the new: two shapes would be two code paths,
  and `validate-config` names the fix for an adopter on the old one.
- `--dev`, landed one cycle ago, retires to `--profile dev`, the treatment the positionals got.
- Multi-step: the placeholder expansion, the schema, the three commands, the retirement, and the
  docs, each reviewable on its own.
- Waiver, wink's "go, complete cycle except for landing on main using the new prototype v0.3.1
  agent-file version" (2026-10-27), after the opening's push.
  - Covers every rung from [1] through the closing: the work review, the description review, the
    per-push approval, and the hard stop after each push.
  - Does not cover Land: the closing is pushed without `--land`, its shape the default,
    trapezoid, until wink chooses at the Land.
  - The v0.3.1 form throughout: two-paragraph bodies ending "See details in zDOING.md.", the rung
    subsection the full account in `*` and `-` form, and the continuation notes in the closing.
  - Validation still runs before every push, and a deviation from the plan is still a stop.

##### feat: a list-valued placeholder expands to its words

`command_list`'s filling learns list values: a word that is a list-valued placeholder alone becomes
its words, none for an empty list.

* A list's words are split before its placeholders are filled, so a value is one word, and an
  empty value would be an empty argument, which cargo refuses.
  - `command_list::expand` takes list values beside the string ones: a word that is `{name}` alone,
    for a list, becomes the list's items, one word each, none for an empty one.
  - `words` stays, the strings-only form, delegating to `expand`, so its callers are unchanged until
    the profile rung passes lists.
* A list inside a longer word, `x{flags}`, has no word for its items to share.
  - It is refused, naming the list and the word, rather than joined with a guessed separator.
* The refusal for an unknown name offered the string placeholders alone.
  - It offers the lists too, so a typo is told every name the list may use.

The commands and `validate-config` name the profile form for each old key, and `init` writes it.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# usage: hooks.sh check|install|test
#
# The Claude Code hooks the agent-files carry, beside this script, installed into
# ~/.claude/hooks and registered in ~/.claude/settings.json (AGENTS.md > Working practices).
#
#   check    each hook installed identical to this copy and registered, else what is not, exit 1
#   install  copy the hooks in and register what is missing, the settings file backed up first
#   test     run bash-guard.sh over commands it must deny or allow
#
# HOOKS_DIR and SETTINGS override the two destinations, for trying install somewhere harmless.
set -euo pipefail
here=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
dest=${HOOKS_DIR:-$HOME/.claude/hooks}
settings=${SETTINGS:-$HOME/.claude/settings.json}
# How a registration names its script: the ~ form settings.json already uses, or the override.
cmd_dir=${HOOKS_DIR:-'~/.claude/hooks'}

scripts=(bash-allow.sh bash-guard.sh inhibit-sleep.sh)

# One registration per line: event, matcher (empty for none), command.
registrations() {
  cat <<EOF
UserPromptSubmit||$cmd_dir/inhibit-sleep.sh start
SubagentStart||$cmd_dir/inhibit-sleep.sh sub-start
SubagentStop||$cmd_dir/inhibit-sleep.sh sub-stop
Stop||$cmd_dir/inhibit-sleep.sh stop
SessionEnd||$cmd_dir/inhibit-sleep.sh end
PreToolUse|Bash|$cmd_dir/bash-allow.sh
PreToolUse|Bash|$cmd_dir/bash-guard.sh
EOF
}

registered() { # event matcher command
  [[ -f $settings ]] || return 1
  jq -e --arg e "$1" --arg m "$2" --arg c "$3" \
    '(.hooks[$e] // []) | any(.[]; (.matcher // "") == $m and any(.hooks[]?; .command == $c))' \
    "$settings" >/dev/null
}

check() {
  local bad=0 s e m c
  for s in "${scripts[@]}"; do
    if [[ ! -f $dest/$s ]]; then
      echo "hooks: missing    $dest/$s"
      bad=1
    elif ! cmp -s "$here/$s" "$dest/$s"; then
      echo "hooks: differs    $dest/$s"
      bad=1
    fi
  done
  while IFS='|' read -r e m c; do
    if ! registered "$e" "$m" "$c"; then
      echo "hooks: unregistered $e${m:+ [$m]}: $c"
      bad=1
    fi
  done < <(registrations)
  if ((bad)); then
    echo "hooks: not installed, run: bash $here/hooks.sh install"
    return 1
  fi
  echo "hooks: ${#scripts[@]} hooks installed and registered"
}

install() {
  local s e m c tmp
  mkdir -p "$dest"
  for s in "${scripts[@]}"; do
    if ! cmp -s "$here/$s" "$dest/$s" 2>/dev/null; then
      cp "$here/$s" "$dest/$s.new"
      chmod +x "$dest/$s.new"
      mv "$dest/$s.new" "$dest/$s"
      echo "hooks: installed  $dest/$s"
    fi
  done
  [[ -f $settings ]] || echo '{}' >"$settings"
  local backed_up=0
  while IFS='|' read -r e m c; do
    registered "$e" "$m" "$c" && continue
    if ((!backed_up)); then
      cp "$settings" "$settings.$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).bak"
      backed_up=1
    fi
    tmp=$(mktemp "$settings.XXXXXX")
    jq --arg e "$e" --arg m "$m" --arg c "$c" '
      {type: "command", command: $c} as $h
      | .hooks //= {} | .hooks[$e] //= []
      | if any(.hooks[$e][]; (.matcher // "") == $m)
        then .hooks[$e] |= map(if (.matcher // "") == $m then .hooks += [$h] else . end)
        else .hooks[$e] += [(if $m == "" then {} else {matcher: $m} end) + {hooks: [$h]}]
        end' "$settings" >"$tmp"
    mv "$tmp" "$settings"
    echo "hooks: registered $e${m:+ [$m]}: $c"
  done < <(registrations)
  check
}

# Each case: the decision bash-guard.sh must make, then the command.
guard_cases() {
  cat <<'EOF'
deny|false; echo rc=$?
deny|vc-x1-dev install --dev 2>&1 | tail -4; echo rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
deny|cargo test 2>&1 | tail -3
deny|cargo test | tail -3; exit ${PIPESTATUS[0]}
deny|cd /home/me/vc-x1; vc-x1 validate | grep FAILED
deny|tmp/candidate/vc-x1 land -s b --dry-run | head
allow|jq -n 1 | grep 1
allow|cargo --version || { rc=$?; echo failed=$rc; exit $rc; }
allow|set -o pipefail; cargo test 2>&1 | tail -3
allow|cd /home/me/vc-x1; jq . f.json | grep x
allow|cargo test -- --include-ignored
allow|vc-x1 validate
allow|echo done
EOF
}

test_guard() {
  local want cmd out got fail=0 n=0
  while IFS='|' read -r want cmd; do
    out=$(jq -n --arg c "$cmd" '{tool_name: "Bash", tool_input: {command: $c}}' |
      bash "$here/bash-guard.sh")
    got=allow
    if [[ -n $out ]]; then
      got=$(jq -r '.hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision' <<<"$out")
    fi
    n=$((n + 1))
    if [[ $got != "$want" ]]; then
      echo "hooks: FAIL want $want, got $got: $cmd"
      fail=1
    fi
  done < <(guard_cases)
  if ((fail)); then
    return 1
  fi
  echo "hooks: bash-guard.sh passed $n cases"
}

case "${1:-}" in
  check) check ;;
  install) install ;;
  test) test_guard ;;
  *)
    echo "usage: hooks.sh check|install|test" >&2
    exit 2
    ;;
esac
